surface: CI workflow dispatch inputs, buildSrc convention plugins, dev-support release scripts, embedded agent jar
boundary: Build/release integrity: workflow input handling, script injection, artifact embedding, release publishing

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted event/input data must never be interpolated directly into run: shells, artifact names, or privileged contexts (workflow expression injection).
local_checks.result: All three workflows interpolate inputs only into run-name/concurrency/if expressions; every run: block that consumes inputs.branch/inputs.run_id/inputs.notes or secrets does so via env vars (build-plugin.yml:603-606 and :670-674; nightly-full.yml:251-254, :352-355, :456-458). inputs.mode is a choice input with fixed options. PowerShell double-quoted interpolation of env var values is not re-executed, so no command/expression injection path found. matrix values are literal lists.

local_checks.invariant: CI authorization: which events trigger privileged workflows, and whether untrusted code (fork PR, issue comment) can reach write tokens.
local_checks.result: push-test.yml triggers only on push to master with permissions contents:read; nightly-full.yml on schedule+workflow_dispatch with contents:read; build-plugin.yml is workflow_dispatch only (requires a caller with write access) with permissions contents:write + actions:read, justified by Release creation and cross-run artifact download. No pull_request/issue_comment/fork-reachable trigger exists. Arbitrary-ref checkout via inputs.branch in build-plugin.yml is reachable only by maintainers who can already dispatch (by-design).

local_checks.invariant: Publish-mode integrity: released bytes must be the bytes a successful gate verified.
local_checks.result: publish mode resolves a source run, requires conclusion==success, requires artifact plugin-<run_number> present, downloads it by run-id, and pins checkout to steps.source.outputs.sha (build-plugin.yml:598-654). The plugin- artifact is only produced by build in gate/release modes whose run success requires the gate aggregate job (all five legs success, :542-579). release mode downloads plugin-<github.run_number> from the same run. Artifact-name-to-run binding is immutable on the actions side. environment: release guards the publish job; whether required reviewers are configured on that environment is a repo-settings fact not visible in source (the workflow comment itself states no reviewers means direct publish).

local_checks.invariant: Secrets must not be echoed, persisted into artifacts, or over-scoped.
local_checks.result: GITHUB_TOKEN is the only credential in build-plugin.yml (GH_TOKEN env, github.token in download-artifact). nightly-full secrets (DIALECT_MATRIX_PROPERTIES, MPV_DB_URL/USER/PASSWORD) enter via env and are written to the runner-local gradle.properties copy (:365-371, :468-475); no artifact uploads gradle.properties (e2e-evidence path is dev-support/e2e-fake-ide/evidence/, dialect summary path is build/reports/...). No hardcoded PAT/keys in workflows; no gitleaks step exists (hardening, no reachable principal).

local_checks.invariant: Gradle properties and paths injected into process command lines must not enable command injection or writes outside the repo from a lower-trust principal.
local_checks.result: All ProcessBuilder sites pass argument lists without a shell (VerifierHomeGuard.kt:37, MemoryWatermark.kt:82, mpv-verification.gradle.kts:531). The one PowerShell script body (VerifierHomeGuard.kt:28-37) is base64 UTF-16LE encoded and interpolates only the verifier home path, which derives from GRADLE_USER_HOME or developer-supplied -PverifierHomeRoot — same principal that runs the build, no boundary crossing. mpv-release writeUpdateManifest (mpv-release.gradle.kts:35-54) writes only inside the repo (update/update.json) from the gradle.properties version; string interpolation into JSON is from a version literal, not external input.

local_checks.invariant: Release tokens must come from gitignored local config, never be hardcoded, logged, or persisted into artifacts; artifact identity must be verified at publish.
local_checks.result: Tokens are read from .local/gitee-token.json / .local/github-token.json with a repo-root fallback; .gitignore excludes .local/*, gitee-token.*, *.token, .secrets/, and git history contains no token files (checked log --all --diff-filter=A). No token is printed; error paths print exception text and API bodies but not request URLs. Gitee v5 API forces token-in-URL/query for GET/DELETE and token-in-multipart for uploads (gitee-release.py:119,136,147; gitee-release-update.py:45,75,91) — server-side URL logging is a Gitee-side fact, not controllable here. Publish integrity: both Gitee scripts do sha256 comparison of the live download URL against the local zip (gitee-release.py:268-292, gitee-release-update.py:129-135), and --from-github requires interactive yes unless --yes.

local_checks.invariant: Composed cmd.exe command lines must not execute content from files or paths a lower-trust principal controls.
local_checks.result: Start-GradleLine (test-shards-parallel.ps1:126-131) composes cmd /c "$gradlew $argsLine ..." where argsLine is built from literal task names, a fixed exclusion table, and class names from dev-support/test-shard-serial-classes.txt (or the caller-supplied -QuarantineFile). The only principals in this flow are the developer running the script and the reviewed repo file — same-principal, no boundary crossing; metacharacters in that file would execute with the developer's own privileges (hardening). push-all.ps1 uses array-form git/curl invocations only (:107, :134). test-shards-parallel.ps1:34 executes a hardcoded out-of-repo absolute path C:\Users\USER\.zcode\cli\parallel_tasks.py at startup (developer-local tool, same principal).

local_checks.invariant: The embedded agent jar must be the agent fat jar produced from the same source tree, with correct task ordering (no stale or partial embedding).
local_checks.result: embedAgentJar (build.gradle.kts:312-324) is a Copy task with from(:sql-visualizer-agent:agentFatJar) which establishes a task-output dependency, so the fat jar is always (re)built before copying; processResources dependsOn embedAgentJar, so resources embedding is ordered after it. A cleaned agent subproject forces regeneration rather than embedding a stale file (Copy from missing task output fails loudly). No checksum/version verification of the embedded jar exists at build time, but the bytes are produced in the same build by construction. No ordering defect found.

local_checks.invariant: Dependencies must be pinned to explicit versions with no dynamic (+, SNAPSHOT, latest) resolution.
local_checks.result: All versions in gradle/libs.versions.toml are explicit literals; plugins in settings.gradle.kts are version-pinned (kotlin 2.3.20, changelog 2.5.0, foojay 1.0.0, IPGP 2.18.1); the only implementation dependency jsqlparser is pinned 5.3 with an explicit exclude. No dynamic versions found. gradle/ contains no verification-metadata.xml (dependency verification absent).

local_checks.invariant: Build inputs (Gradle distribution, dependency jars) must come from a trusted root with independent integrity verification; a mirror that can differ from the canonical source must not silently feed release builds.
local_checks.result: Two unverified third-party sources are configured: (1) gradle-wrapper.properties:3 points the Gradle 9.7.0 distribution at mirrors.cloud.tencent.com with no distributionSha256Sum; (2) settings.gradle.kts:50 places https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public before mavenCentral (:52) for all dependency resolution, with no dependency verification file. Every workflow rewrites the wrapper URL to services.gradle.org on CI (e.g. build-plugin.yml:100-103), demonstrating the authors treat the mirror as not equally trusted, yet the dependency mirror remains active on CI release builds and neither mirror is verified anywhere. Recorded as candidates.

local_checks.invariant: The marketplace/compat gate must run the pinned verifier-cli version; the pin must be enforced at the resolution site, not assumed.
local_checks.result: CI seeds the pinned jar (dev-support/verifier-cli-version.txt = 1.411) into GRADLE_USER_HOME/caches/modules-2/files-2.1/org.jetbrains.intellij.plugins/verifier-cli/ci-seed/ (build-plugin.yml:319-331, :397-409). All three gate consumers resolve the jar via walkTopDown().maxDepth(4) .filter{name matches verifier-cli-*-all.jar}.firstOrNull() with no version comparison (mpv-verification.gradle.kts:203-206, :356-359, :480-483); the CI seed dir and normal Gradle version dirs coexist under the same module dir and setup-gradle caches persist older jars across runs. The only guard (VerifierCliVersionGuardTest) asserts pinned ∈ cached set (passes with extra versions) and skips when the cache is empty or on CI (its own docs, :18-19, :38, :46). The repo's own comment records that this walk already picked an unintended older version once (mpv-verification.gradle.kts:127-131) and that verdict outcomes differ between 1.409/1.410. Recorded as candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Repo agent-instruction files or hooks must not execute repo scripts with secrets in env outside the reviewed CI paths.
local_checks.result: AGENTS.md is 13 lines of contributor policy with no hook definitions, no secret references, and no script executions; .zcode config is not tracked (gitignored). No repo-level hooks found.

All third-party actions are referenced by floating major tags (actions/checkout@v6, actions/setup-java@v5, actions/upload-artifact@v7, actions/download-artifact@v8, gradle/actions/setup-gradle@v5, actions/cache@v6); pinning to commit SHAs would bound tag-hijack exposure of the contents:write release workflow.

writeUpdateManifest (buildSrc/src/main/kotlin/mpv-release.gradle.kts:35-54) emits update/update.json with version/downloadUrl/changeNotes/publishDate/sinceBuild but no artifact sha256 or size; gitee-release.py's sha256 verification is local-only at publish time and never published, so the Gitee self-update channel binds only a mutable URL (consumer-side behavior is owned by the update-chain unit).

test-shards-parallel.ps1:126-131 composes a cmd /c command line from dev-support/test-shard-serial-classes.txt contents; no lower-trust principal exists in this flow today, but keeping that file free of cmd metacharacters (or switching to array-form invocation) removes the latent same-principal injection surface.

test-shards-parallel.ps1:34 executes a hardcoded out-of-repo absolute path (C:\Users\USER\.zcode\cli\parallel_tasks.py); referencing a repo-relative or configurable path avoids silently executing whatever exists at that machine-specific location.

gitee-release.py / gitee-release-update.py / mirror-releases-to-github.py pass the Gitee token as URL query parameter or multipart field, as required by the Gitee v5 API; prefer header-based auth where the API allows to reduce server/proxy URL-log exposure.

No secret-scanning (gitleaks etc.) workflow exists; .gitignore coverage of gitee-token.*, .local/*, *.token, .secrets/ is correct and no token files appear in git history, so this is hardening only.

local_checks.result: No Runtime.getRuntime().exec, ProcessBuilder, or javax.script usage in src/main or agent main. The only 'eval' is the closed OGNL-subset evaluator (xml/Ognl.kt) over mapper XML values — no dynamic class loading or command execution; owned in depth by the injection unit.

local_checks.invariant: Browser-open targets must not be attacker-influenceable to a different origin (open redirect)
local_checks.result: All browse targets are fixed https constants (UpdateSource.MARKETPLACE_URL/GITEE_RELEASES_URL, FeedbackApi.SITE_BASE) except FeedbackApi.detailUrl(postNo):165 which interpolates a server-returned postNo into a fixed-origin query string, and ErrorReportDialog.browserFallback:469-473 which URLEncoder-encodes ideVersion/pluginVersion into a fixed-origin query. The host cannot be changed by the interpolated value (it sits after scheme+host); worst case is extra query/fragment text on the plugin's own site. No open redirect to a foreign origin.

local_checks.invariant: TLS enforced for all shipped network URLs
local_checks.result: Every shipped URL (update manifest/download on gitee.com raw/releases, feedback sql-visualizer.jvtools.cn, docs/help/about/marketplace, plugin.xml vendor/description links) is https://. The only http:// literals are XML parser feature URIs (SecureXml.kt:71-77) which are JAXP constants, not network endpoints. No plaintext HTTP endpoint in shipped code.

local_checks.invariant: Error paths must not leak stack traces or internals to users/agents beyond the known feedback flow
local_checks.result: MCP tool errors are structured constant codes with bounded messages (McpToolErrors.kt); no printStackTrace/stackTraceToString in src/main. ConnectionErrorClassifier maintains an exclusion-signature list including 'password'/'access denied' for error classification. The feedback-composer path (ErrorReportComposer includes OS/plugin version, user-reviewed body) is the known documented flow. No additional leak path found.

local_checks.invariant: Exported HTML report files must HTML-escape every field derived from lower-trust input (SQL text, project-file metadata) because the plugin writes the report to disk and auto-opens it in the external browser via BrowserUtil.open
local_checks.result: SqlPreviewPanel.currentTableName() flows unescaped into 'Table: $it' at HtmlReportFormatter.kt:72 and dialect at :73; parameter source names flow unescaped into '$src' at :147 (only the paired value is escaped). SQL tokens, plain text segments and param values are escaped (escapeHtml at :91/:97/:107/:147). The sibling diagnostic HTML export (DiagnosticReportFormatter.formatHtml) escapes the entire metaLine that contains tableName/source/dialect (DiagnosticReportFormatter.kt:164) and every list line (:256), proving intent and leaving HtmlReportFormatter as the inconsistent variant. ShareDialog.exportHtmlReport auto-opens the written file with BrowserUtil.open(file.toURI()) (ShareDialog.kt:219), as does exportDiagnosticHtml (:195). Existing HtmlReportFormatterTest only asserts escaping of SQL text, not of tableName or source names.

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust project-file metadata (mapper XML, entity annotations, hbm/pages XML) reaching PreviewResult.tableName / unresolvedParams is charset-validated before it reaches renderers
local_checks.result: No validation. EntityResolver.annotationValue returns the raw @TableName/@TableField string literal (EntityResolver.kt:101, :454-472) with no charset restriction, and PreviewResult.tableName is populated from it (SqlPreviewService.kt:239/:511, PagesXmlPreviewService.kt:204/:222). CrudSqlGenerator builds unresolvedParams from entity column names (:167) which come from the same arbitrary annotation strings. Counter-evidence checked: console/log capture paths always set tableName=null and synthetic 'paramN' sources (LogEntryPreviewRecognizer.kt:168/:186/:218/:235, LiteralParamRecovery.kt:207); HQL named params are regex-restricted to [a-zA-Z0-9_] (SqlPreviewService.kt:733/:1313); so the arbitrary-string reach is specifically via project-file metadata (mapper XML / entity annotations), which the trust model classifies as a lower-trust principal.

local_checks.invariant: The reflection-based ACP transport registrar must not load or execute attacker-influenced code, only register a fixed behavior onto the ml-llm EP
local_checks.result: Safe: Class.forName targets two fixed compile-time constants (AcpTransportRegistrar.kt:89-91); the dynamic proxy dispatches getTransport by method name and returns a reflectively-resolved enum constant or null; no user/code-supplied class names, no XML-declared classes, guarded by optional-depends on com.intellij.ml.llm and runCatching; effect is limited to giving claude-acp agent sessions the SSE transport for the platform MCP server (an MCP-surface question owned elsewhere, registration itself introduces no new sink).

local_checks.invariant: Generated Wrapper/Java code embeds untrusted SQL-derived strings with Java string escaping so hostile console/SQL text cannot alter generated-code structure
local_checks.result: Mostly held: javaEscape/javaString (:1336-1350) is applied to Condition.Raw templates (apply("...")), values (javaValue :1219-1230), column refs (renderColumnRef :986), LIMIT tails and join strings. Two raw interpolations remain: deleteTargets joined as '"$it"' (:518) and subQuery alias in t.setAlias("${subQuery.alias}") (:315), both SQL identifiers that can contain quotes via quoted identifiers; impact is a malformed/never-compiling generated snippet that the developer sees in full in the panel before copying, so recorded as hardening rather than a boundary crossing.

local_checks.invariant: Feedback upload path uses fixed endpoints, bounded reads, and only sends user-consented content
local_checks.result: Held: fixed HTTPS base (FeedbackApi.kt:35-38), 10s timeouts, 2MB bounded read incl. gzip-bomb cap (readBounded :318-329), error bodies only surfaced as user messages, deferred queue is memory-only and enqueued strictly after user confirmation (PendingReportScheduler.kt KDoc :21-27), server message shown via describeHttpFailure with non-JSON bodies only truncated to 80 chars for display.

local_checks.invariant: Rollback plan generation and SQL temp-file handling leave no persistent or shared-world artifacts
local_checks.result: RollbackSnapshotStore is in-memory LRU with bounded entries and synchronous index pruning; no temp files in rollback generation. DatabaseConsoleLauncher writes executed SQL (which can carry literal parameter values) to a temp file via FileUtil.createTempFile('mpsql-exec-', '.sql', true) with deleteOnExit; content stays in the user's temp directory with default file perms — hardening note only (sensitive literal values in a world-readable temp file would need a non-default local setup).

local_checks.invariant: Decompiled-platform mcpStub signatures must not be packaged into the plugin artifact
local_checks.result: Held: mcpStub source set compiles to an output dir attached only to compileKotlin.libraries and test classpaths (build.gradle.kts:234-245); comments state and wiring confirms it is excluded from runtime and packaging because com.intellij.mcpserver.* classes would collide with platform 253+/262 built-ins.

local_checks.invariant: Dev-support local servers and release helpers must not expose network-reachable or injectable surfaces
local_checks.result: Both local servers bind 127.0.0.1 only (local-manifest-server.py:73, hotswap-local-server.py:105); gitee-release.py invokes git via subprocess.run with argument list, no shell string interpolation found. These scripts are developer-only tooling, not shipped in the plugin artifact.

surface: Imported settings JSON (shared/team files) and plugin settings fields
boundary: Settings-to-SQL boundary: tenant column, logic-delete values, table-name rules flow into rendered/executed SQL

excluded_blocks.reason: No HTTP server or sessions in a desktop plugin

local_checks.invariant: Imported settings JSON can only change SQL-affecting fields (logicDeleteValue, tenantColumnName, tenantColumnDefault, dataPermissionMockCondition, dynamicTableNameRules, tablePrefix/Suffix) within a validated whitelist, and the version gate blocks newer formats
local_checks.result: Whitelist merge (SettingsIO.kt:91-113) controls which keys are accepted but performs zero content validation on the 24 accepted fields, five-plus of which are concatenated into rendered SQL downstream; version gate (SettingsIO.kt:82-86) requires a version field and rejects version > 1 — no bypass found, but fractional versions truncate (1.9 toInt() == 1) so a forward-version file is accepted as current. Per task note, peer already verified autosave path/pattern fields are excluded from the whitelist (relied upon, not re-derived).

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust channels that set SQL-affecting settings (imported shared file, VCS-shared project settings) present the same or greater friction than direct UI configuration
local_checks.result: Two lower-trust channels confirmed: (1) settings-file import (PluginSettingsPanel.kt:1695-1721) reads an arbitrary .json file chosen by the operator and merges into the live global state with no diff/preview of SQL-affecting values; (2) project-level settings persist to .idea/mp-sql-visualizer-project.xml (ProjectPluginSettings.kt:21-24) — routinely committed to VCS — carrying logicDeleteValue/tablePrefix/tableSuffix that override global values when useProjectSettings is set (ProjectPluginSettings.kt:115-132). No system-property override exists for these SQL-affecting fields in config/ (only user.home for file choosers).

local_checks.invariant: Each settings field entering rendered SQL stays within its syntactic position (tenant column = identifier, logic-delete/tenant values = single literal, mock condition = WHERE fragment, table-name rule = identifier)
local_checks.result: No positional enforcement at any injection site: logicDeleteValue and tenantColumnDefault become SqlValue.Literal(raw) (SqlPreviewServiceEnhancements.kt:386,393,403,420; SqlPreviewService.kt:404-406; TenantLineEnhancer.kt:41-46) rendered verbatim by SqlGenerator; tenantColumnName becomes a ColumnRef rendered through dialect.quoteIfKeyword only (quotes reserved words, otherwise raw — Dialect.kt:72-73, ColumnRef.kt:39-40); dataPermissionMockCondition becomes Condition.Raw appended to WHERE (DataPermissionPlaceholder.kt:43-51, rendered verbatim at SqlGenerator.kt:513-521); dynamicTableNameRules replacement text replaces the table-name model field raw (SqlPreviewService.kt:1496-1506, DynamicTableNameProcessor.kt:61-68). Any of these values can carry arbitrary SQL text (OR/UNION/comments/semicolons) into the rendered statement.

local_checks.invariant: The SQL renderer escapes or delimits model values so that a value cannot change statement semantics
local_checks.result: Renderer is pass-through by design: SqlValue.Literal renders value.raw with no quoting/escaping (SqlValue.kt:20-23 documents raw as 'rendered into SQL verbatim'; SqlGenerator.kt:559-560, 485); Condition.Raw renders sqlText verbatim (SqlGenerator.kt:513-521); table names and column identifiers are quoted only when they collide with a dialect reserved word (SqlGenerator.kt:554; Dialect.kt:72-73). The strongest source-visible control for this boundary is the SettingsIO key whitelist, which does not address content.

local_checks.invariant: SQL reaching the execute path does not carry settings-injected fragments that the operator did not see configured, and the CRUD generator does not interpolate settings values
local_checks.result: The preview panel submits its rendered/editor SQL text to SqlExecutor.execute (SqlExecutor.kt:38-93) — settings-injected fragments are part of that text and reach execution behind the standard datasource-picker/DML confirms; no re-validation of injected fragment content occurs in this path (deeper execute-side gates are peer-owned). CrudSqlGenerator does not interpolate logicDeleteValue/tenant settings (hardcoded literal 1 at CrudSqlGenerator.kt:138; identifiers via dialect.quoteIfNeeded) — no settings sink there.

local_checks.invariant: Exported settings JSON does not leak credentials/tokens/secrets
local_checks.result: exportToJson (SettingsIO.kt:30-57) emits only the 24 override fields; PluginSettings.State holds no datasource credentials, tokens, or keys (datasource credentials live in the IDE platform, not this State), and history/param data (paramHistoryJson, paramSchemesJson) and feedback identity (reportSubmitterEmail) are excluded. No secret-leak finding.

surface: Executable SQL text in the preview panel, replay, rollback plan, and CRUD generation reaching user datasources
boundary: Execution authorization: dialect gate, DML confirms, unbounded-write detector bypass, schema/timeout gates

local_checks.invariant: Every non-query (DML/DDL/UNKNOWN per SqlTypeClassifier) UI execution requires a YesNo confirm whose message escalates through ExecuteConfirmMessages/UnboundedWriteDetector findings
local_checks.result: Confirmed on all three production entry points (SqlPreviewPanelExecution.executeSql :1144-1157, executeAdhocSql :434-454, LogToSqlPanel.executeSql :341-356). The dmlConfirmed=true exemption in executeAdhocSql has no production caller (grep: only RollbackSqlPanelTest). isQuery requires ALL statements of a batch to classify QUERY, with a fail-closed read-only second proof (proveReadOnly blocks writable CTE, EXPLAIN ANALYZE+DML, SELECT INTO OUTFILE/identifier), so mixed batches always get the confirm.

local_checks.invariant: UnboundedWriteDetector parse-failure path must not fail open for UPDATE/DELETE (candidate attack (b))
local_checks.result: Disproved: detect() catches parse exceptions and returns Finding(PARSE_FAILED) which is dangerous=true (kind != SUBQUERY), so ExecuteConfirmMessages renders the escalated execute.confirm.unbounded.summary; SqlAstParser additionally converts JSqlParser 5.3's silent null return into a thrown JSQLParserException so null cannot bypass the catch. Parse failure strengthens, not weakens, the confirm.

local_checks.invariant: Unknown render/target dialect blocks writes and requires explicit confirm for queries, evaluated against the actual session/console datasource
local_checks.result: allowDialectGate runs twice per submission (session creation in continuePrepareAfterTempFile sessionConsumer, and again from the live JdbcConsole at the top of executeOnConsole before any document mutation). RAW/unknown-render DML and EXPLAIN are BLOCKED (RENDER_UNKNOWN_BLOCK/TARGET_UNKNOWN_BLOCK); queries get showYesNoDialog. MANUAL_CONFLICT and RERENDER_UNAVAILABLE intentionally allow execution with a status hint (documented user decision 2026-10-25: dialect conflict does not veto execution when both dialects are known) — a deliberate policy, not a bypass.

local_checks.invariant: Execution cannot silently land on a different datasource than the bound/confirmed target (candidate attack (e): alias resolution, last-used fallback, flipped console)
local_checks.result: Reuse of the shared console is identity-based: ExecFileBinding.resolveSharedConsoleReuse requires the live console UUID to equal the intended UUID; identity unresolvable = no reuse (fail-closed); learned-vs-last-used conflict returns null and forces the picker; ambiguous last-used memory is dropped, not guessed. Residual: when no UUID identity is resolvable at all, reuse falls back to legacy display-name equality (legacyMemoryName == legacySharedRecordedName), which two same-named datasources can satisfy; and realignExecBind silently rewrites the platform per-file pin to the memory/learned target when it differs from a native pin. Both are same-principal heuristics with a binding indicator, recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: EXPLAIN path cannot turn a write-effective or non-whitelisted statement into an unconfirmed execution (candidate attack (c): EXPLAIN executing raw statement)
local_checks.result: ExplainGate.planExplainSubmit only wraps statements whose first keyword is in {select, values, table, with} (word-boundary check); anything else returns NotExplainable and does not submit. EXPLAIN ANALYZE + DML, SELECT INTO OUTFILE/INTO <table>, and writable CTEs are reclassified UNKNOWN by SqlTypeClassifier.proveReadOnly so they cannot ride the query exemption. EXPLAIN still passes the ${} raw-segment and unknown-param confirm gates. DmlImpactEstimator probes are single SELECT COUNT(*) statements that must pass the MCP SELECT whitelist (test-pinned).

local_checks.invariant: Every execution affordance the plugin hosts in the preview console applies the same execution-authorization chain (dialect gate, DML confirm, unbounded-write detector) (candidate attacks (a)/(c)/(d))
local_checks.result: VIOLATION for the native affordance: prepareAfterEditorResolved (DataSourceSelectorConsole.kt :246-350) injects a UiDataProvider supplying PROJECT, EDITOR, VIRTUAL_FILE, PSI_FILE and the DBN SessionClientHolder.CLIENT_KEY, and installs the native Console.Jdbc.Left/Right header via JdbcConsole.buildHeaderComponent specifically so the native Execute (▶) action and Ctrl+Enter are enabled inside the plugin's embedded preview console. That path executes the console document directly through the platform (the code itself enumerates it as one of three execution paths: '原生 ▶ / 控制台 Ctrl+Enter / 插件按钮') and contains none of the plugin gates — SqlTypeClassifier confirm, ExecuteConfirmMessages/UnboundedWriteDetector, SchemaValidationGate, allowDialectGate are only in the plugin-button chain (executeSql/executeAdhocSql/LogToSqlPanel). The plugin's own Execute button on the same panel requires all of them for the same document text, which is derived from console/log capture (the lower-trust principal this chain exists for). Proposed as needs_validation candidate.

local_checks.invariant: SQL text shown to the confirm dialog equals the text actually submitted (candidate attack (a): any transformation between display and execution)
local_checks.result: Fast path re-syncs nativeEditorDoc to the confirmed sql via WriteCommandAction before executePrepared; full chain writes the same submitSql into mpsql-exec.sql and executeOnConsole re-reads editor.document.text as executedSql. Two divergences exist by design or by race: (1) MysqlClientGSuffix strips a trailing \G between confirm (shows original) and submission — line-anchored, literal-safe, documented two-state separation, benign; (2) TOCTOU: executeOnConsole re-reads editor.document.text after the modal confirm, and the native submission is an asynchronous TransactionGuard.submitTransactionLater whose delay the code documents up to ~6.7s, so text changed in the editable embedded console between confirm and submission (by the user, or by plugin doc writers such as attachResultsHook contentAdded rewrite) executes without re-confirmation. No non-user write primitive into that document was found; recorded as hardening rather than a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Confirm-dialog state machine and multi-statement batching cannot execute statements beyond the confirmed set (candidate attack (d): double-click, whole-script override)
local_checks.result: wholeScriptExec (ExecOption override to EXECUTE_INSIDE_WHOLE_SCRIPT, DataSourceSelector.wholeScriptExecOption :1207-1216) is only set by executeAdhocSql when IdentityInsertStatements.containsStatement(sql) matches the plugin's own rollback batches, and the confirm dialog for that path displays the full batch text, so the confirmed set equals the executed set. PrepareSingleFlightGate serializes prepare chains and consumes queued intents with their own confirmed callbacks; executionGeneration invalidates stale submissions; double-click yields two separately confirmed submissions rather than one confirmed + one blind. Residual: dollarRawConfirmedInSession and unknownParamsConfirmedInSession are panel-session sticky — one YES suppresses the raw-segment/unknown-param warnings for all later, potentially different SQL in the same panel (the DML confirm itself still re-runs). Hardening.

local_checks.invariant: Parallel/legacy execution entries (CRUD/table templates, history replay, DatabaseConsoleLauncher temp-file path) apply equivalent gates (candidate attack (c))
local_checks.result: Table template actions render only read-only SELECT/EXPLAIN templates and validatedTableIdentifier rejects ';', '--', '/*' and control chars, so isQuery=true passed to SqlExecutor.execute is honest. History package has no direct SqlExecutor entry (grep). DatabaseConsoleLauncher.execute only creates a temp mpsql-exec-*.sql under the system temp dir and opens it in the editor — the user picks the datasource and executes via IDE-native interaction; it performs no execution itself and the temp file is created by the platform FileUtil with a random suffix (no prediction issue for a same-principal desktop model).

surface: Autosave history files on disk (user-configurable dir and name pattern)
boundary: Path construction boundary: settings-derived file name pattern and save dir -> file write; reader re-parses files

local_checks.invariant: Settings-derived saveDir and fileNamePattern are canonicalized/rejected before path construction and file write
local_checks.result: No sanitization found: resolveFileName (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:538-550) only replaces ':' with '-', so '..' segments, '/' separators and UNC prefixes (\\host\share\f.sql) survive; currentFileName (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:454-465) treats any name containing File.separator as a full path and otherwise prepends saveDir, so traversal out of saveDir is possible for operator-set patterns; resolveHistoryDir (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:626-630) honors an arbitrary customPath verbatim. Cross-principal setting injection is disproved: SettingsIO.importFromJson (SettingsIO.kt:80-115) whitelist does not include logAutoSavePath/logAutoSaveFileNamePattern/logAutoSaveMaxFiles, and the only other writer is the operator's own settings state (SqlLogManager.kt:524-532). Traversal therefore requires the operator configuring it himself: same-principal, recorded as hardening, not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: Autosave append path refuses symlinked or non-regular-file targets, at parity with the revision-append path (fileKey NOFOLLOW + isRegularFile + !isSymbolicLink CAS at SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:98-102,130,139)
local_checks.result: openWriterForCurrent (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:436-451) opens with Files.newBufferedWriter(CREATE, APPEND) without LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS and without any regular-file/symlink check, so a symlink planted at the configured saveDir/fileName (both inside the project by default) is followed and plugin-formatted entry text (header + restoredSql derived from untrusted console text + Base64 pd line, SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:486-529) is appended to an attacker-chosen target outside the project. The defensive asymmetry with the merge path is source-visible; recorded as needs_validation candidate fingerprint history.autosave.append-open-symlink-follow.

local_checks.invariant: Read-back bounds cap per-file and per-line memory before parsing (100MB cap named in unit description)
local_checks.result: No reader-side size bound exists: readFromFile/forEachEntry (SqlLogFileReader.kt:136-145,234-257) and countInFile (162-182) check only file existence; the 100MB roll threshold is writer-side only (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:31). boundedLines (SqlLogFileReader.kt:99-118) collapses only lines starting with REVISION_PREFIX ('-- pd: o147-revision: '); any other line of arbitrary size is fully buffered in a StringBuilder, EntryBlockScanner (265-313) accumulates the whole block, parseBlockLines:336 joins a second full copy, and the pd line (324-332) Base64-decodes and JSON-parses further full copies. Recorded as needs_validation candidate fingerprint history.reader.unbounded-line-buffering.

local_checks.invariant: Retention prune (pruneRetainedFiles) deletes only this plugin's name-family files and cannot be steered into deleting unrelated user files
local_checks.result: Settled safe within this boundary: buildFamilyRegex (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:306-325) requires at least one literal segment, matches full basename, and prune filters dir .sql files by familyRegex before grouping/deletion (266-293); deletion candidates are limited to family-matching names in the operator-configured dir, and any principal able to influence that outcome already has write/delete access to the same directory (direct deletion is equally available), so no privilege gain. Case-folding of extension and lastModified-based ordering are noted but do not cross a boundary.

surface: Console/log text of any hosted run console
boundary: Parse-pairing/replay state machine: Preparing/Parameters pairing, multi-line continuation, replay guard

local_checks.invariant: Console filter rehighlight replays must be dropped, not re-ingested as new entries (replay guard idempotency)
local_checks.result: ConsoleReplayGuard.decide enforces a per-console watermark + document-stamp + line-0 comparison (lines 53-73); guard is per BridgeLineContext, generation-guarded stale proxies exit in handleConsoleLine (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:391-430); guard degrades fail-open only when editor reflection is unavailable (attachReplayGuard, lines 503-530). No source path lets console text influence watermark/stamp decisions.

local_checks.invariant: A thread's Parameters must never be paired with another thread's Preparing SQL (interleaved-thread pairing state machine)
local_checks.result: All four parsers route lines through per-thread-token buckets (LogThreadRouter, max 64 buckets, idle eviction); bridge contexts are per-console (BridgeLineContext) and handleConsoleLine synchronizes on ctx. Control fails open when threadTokenOf returns null (no level keyword/bracket segment in line): token-less lines share one fallback bucket with single-slot pendingSql/pendingParams, restoring the original cross-thread mispairing for log formats without log-framework prefixes. Candidate log.threadrouter.failopen-fallback-cross-thread-param-mixing records this residual.

local_checks.invariant: Entries pending in per-thread buckets must eventually flush even when the thread never logs again (settle flush completeness)
local_checks.result: flushSettled is implemented and invoked (per-line SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1165-1166 and EDT flushSettledEntries :447-488) only for JdbcTemplateLogParser and ShardingSphereLogParser. MyBatisLogParser and HibernateLogParser have no settled flush and no periodic closePending on the live capture path, so their buckets holding pendingSql/collecting stay non-idle indefinitely (see candidate log.threadrouter.unbounded-nonidle-bucket-retention).

local_checks.invariant: Bridge and EP dual channels must not double-produce or corrupt shared parser state (capture gate state machine)
local_checks.result: EP and bridge hold separate BridgeLineContext instances (SqlConsoleBridgeFilterProvider.kt:43-66 vs SqlLogConsoleBridge.attachFilter:324-343), so concurrent parsing cannot cross-contaminate state; epActive short-circuits the bridge only after the EP demonstrably produced an entry (SqlCaptureGate, SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:885-896, EP set at SqlConsoleBridgeFilterProvider.kt:94-96); duplicate window entries fall under buffer dedupe (SqlLogEntryBuffer dedupeKey/crossChannelKey, entries capped at DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES=200, eviction at :467). Transient double-produce is folded by dedupe, not a state-corruption path.

local_checks.invariant: Sad-path inputs (empty/oversized/malformed/duplicate Preparing/Parameters, blank lines, prefix-only lines, mixed foreign statements) must not produce entries with foreign SQL or swallowed log lines
local_checks.result: MyBatisLogParser handles prefix-only waits (branches 2/3/5), rejects empty-parameter swallowing via looksLikeLogLine re-feed (branch 3, :113-128), terminates continuation on blank/log/foreign lines (branch 6, :161-168), truncates pendingSql to maxParseLength, and discards interceptor self-path markers (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1120-1129). Residual: prefix-only 'Parameters:' between statements leaves the prior pendingSql open as continuation target (branch 3 gives up the wait without closePending), bounded by looksLikeLogLine/foreign-statement guards on continuation content; no foreign-SQL entry constructed from these states.

hunter_hardening: SqlErrorLineRecognizer caps the error-block continuation (4000 chars / 30 lines) but the block-opening line is stored uncapped (firstLineText) and retained on the buffer entry via bindErrorToRecent; truncating the first line to MAX_ERROR_TEXT_LENGTH would bound per-entry error memory.

surface: Console/log text of any hosted run console
boundary: Parser trust boundary: untrusted log text becomes executable SQL, navigation targets, stored entries

excluded_blocks.reason: No browser DOM; panel rendering is Swing non-HTML

local_checks.invariant: Restored parameter values must remain data (quoted/escaped), never re-parsed as SQL structure, and ? replacement must be string-aware
local_checks.result: LogSqlRestorer.restore replaces ? positions from placeholderPositions (string-aware: skips '...' with '' escapes and comments); renderParam quotes non-plain types with '' escaping (LogSqlRestorer.kt:91), PLAIN_TYPES/date-family raw literals are validated by NUMERIC_REGEX/DATE_RE/TS_RE before emission; cardinality mismatch only annotates, never mis-substitutes (PlaceholderCardinality). The log text itself remains fully attacker-writable (they can author any Preparing line), so quoting is a fidelity control, not a privilege boundary; no path lets a parameter value escape quoting into SQL structure via the ?-positional chain.

local_checks.invariant: Named-parameter substitution must not let one parameter's value text re-enter substitution as a :name token (second-order injection into restored SQL)
local_checks.result: JdbcTemplateLogParser.replaceNamedParams (:299-307) performs sequential plain String.replace of ":name" over one shared mutable result. A value containing another parameter's name token (or prefix-overlapping names like :a vs :ab) is re-substituted, producing restored SQL that diverges from any faithful rendering (value-to-value confusion, placeholder corruption). Quoting keeps every substituted value a quoted literal, so a quoting breakout into arbitrary SQL was not establishable from source; recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted console marker text (SQLVIS-SOURCE path/line) must only navigate within project content roots and never govern privileged operations
local_checks.result: SqlSourceMarker.parse validates prefix, segment count 2-4, non-blank path, numeric line; interceptor self-path markers are dropped with a defense log (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1120-1129). SourcePathResolver.resolveVirtualFile (:94-114) joins the marker-derived relative path to project base/content/source roots and opens the result via LocalFileSystem, without rejecting '..' or absolute components and without verifying containment in a root (hardening: same-principal navigation only - the operator can open any local file; jump target feeds editor navigation, not execution or file reads).

local_checks.invariant: Paste/convert and literal-recovery paths must bound work and keep round-trip fidelity of literal parameters
local_checks.result: recoverLiteralParams caps at MAX_RECOVERED_PARAMS=32, uses a linear scanner with comment/string awareness, and requires verifyLiteralRoundTrip-style self-consistency (placeholder count gate :205); LogToSqlPanel routes heavy inputs (>1M chars or >=1k lines) to a cancelable background task (:424-444) and feeds the same bounded parsers. No injection sink beyond the panel editor text.

local_checks.invariant: Untrusted restored SQL reaches the execution sink only through the same user-confirmed entry the panel shows
local_checks.result: Entry execution passes entry.restoredSql (SqlLogPanelActions.kt:108) into the execute subsystem's DataSourceSelector/confirm gates (peer-owned unit); no hidden path in the log-capture subsystem invokes execution autonomously on capture.

boundary: Bounded-resource boundary: parse length caps, error-block caps, buffer growth, regex cost on untrusted text

local_checks.invariant: Per-line parse work must be bounded on untrusted console text (length caps applied at every parser intake)
local_checks.result: SQL bodies are truncated to maxParseLength in all four parsers (MyBatisLogParser.kt:87,152,183-191; HibernateLogParser multiline bounded :164,224,242; JdbcTemplateLogParser appendCollecting bound :367 and take() at :129,252,393; ShardingSphere actual-lines capped by MAX_ACTUAL_LINES=64 plus joined-length counter :84-92). Exceptions: MyBatisLogParser Parameters text reaches parseParams untruncated (branch 4 :131-141 and branch 3 :125) and finishEntries parses the full raw line with ExecutionTimeParser (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1186) - the two candidate regex-cost findings below.

local_checks.invariant: Error-block aggregation must be bounded (length and line caps) and the hot-path recognizer must stay regex-free
local_checks.result: isErrorLine is an O(vocabulary x line) contains list with no regex (SqlErrorLineRecognizer.kt:70-76, guarded by LogRouterHotPathRegexGuardTest); continuation aggregation enforces MAX_ERROR_TEXT_LENGTH=4000 and MAX_ERROR_STACK_LINES=30 (SqlLogConsoleBridge.kt:1136-1143). Gap (hardening): the block-opening line itself is stored uncapped (firstLineText :95, pendingError init :1146) and is retained on the buffer entry via bindErrorToRecent, so a single multi-hundred-KB console line lands in memory per error entry; buffer entries are capped at 200, bounding total exposure to 200 x console-line-length.

local_checks.invariant: Auxiliary per-line parsers (timestamp, table, thread-token) must be linear on unbounded lines and bucket/cardinality state must be capped
local_checks.result: LogTimestampParser patterns are start-anchored (^) with non-MULTILINE find, so non-matching positions fail O(1); SqlTableExtractor TABLE_REGEX is a simple literal-anchored scan; threadTokenOf uses bounded 35-char windows around the level keyword. Bucket cardinality is capped at 64 with idle eviction, but eviction cannot remove buckets held non-idle by pendingSql/collecting state in MyBatis/Hibernate parsers (no settled flush) - see candidate log.threadrouter.unbounded-nonidle-bucket-retention.

local_checks.invariant: Captured-entry buffer must have an aggregate cap and cleanup
local_checks.result: SqlLogEntryBuffer enforces maxEntries (DEFAULT_MAX_ENTRIES=200) with head eviction and index re-pointing (:467-497), so panel-side accumulation is bounded; growth risk concentrates in per-console parser buckets (candidate below).

surface: Re-imported autosave .sql history files (writable by anything with project-dir access)
boundary: Second-order trust: file content written by capture pipeline is re-read, re-parsed and re-executed

local_checks.invariant: Re-parsed history entries carry a source-visible integrity or provenance distinction before they reach the preview/execute chain
local_checks.result: No integrity check exists: any *.sql in the history dir (default inside the project, .idea/sql-visualizer/sql-history) is parsed identically to plugin-written files; the pd payload's 'pv'/'s' keys let a planted file forge captureProvenance/source (SqlLogParamCodec.kt:166-167,234-239) so planted entries are indistinguishable from captured ones. The re-execution chain (HistorySqlLogPanel.showFileContent:518-544 -> entry preview -> LogToSqlPanel.executeSql:341-368 -> SqlExecutor.execute) applies the same non-SELECT YesNo confirm showing the SQL and the dialect gate as freshly captured SQL, and SELECTs execute without per-query confirm exactly as in the normal feature, so the chain itself is not a privilege gain; the gap is that reader output is trusted wholesale. Recorded as hardening; the exploitable amplification of this chain is consolidated into history.reader.unbounded-line-buffering.

local_checks.invariant: AI-agent-triggered history search (sqlv_history_search) bounds total memory work over the planted-file directory
local_checks.result: HistorySearchService caps entries (MAX_SCAN_ENTRIES=200000, HistorySearchService.kt:60,147-162) and preview size, but entry-count caps do not bound bytes per entry: SqlLogFileReader.forEachEntry feeds the same unbounded boundedLines/EntryBlockScanner path, so one planted .sql with a single huge non-revision line defeats the cap and exhausts IDE heap on an agent-triggered read. Same root cause as candidate fingerprint history.reader.unbounded-line-buffering; not a separate finding.

local_checks.invariant: sourceFile header comment from a planted history file cannot direct jump-to-source outside project roots
local_checks.result: EntrySourceMatcher.normalize (EntrySourceMatcher.kt:52-53,71-72) only trims and converts backslashes; it does not collapse '..' segments, and SourcePathResolver.resolveVirtualFile (EntrySourceMatcher.kt:94-113) string-concatenates base/root + rel, so a planted header 'source: ../../<path>' resolves files outside the project on a user-initiated jump. Effect is limited to opening a file in the IDE editor the user can already open (same-principal read, explicit user click), so recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Corrupted/huge Base64-JSON pd payloads and revision lines cannot allocate unbounded memory or poison subsequent entries
local_checks.result: Revision path is well bounded: Revisions.offer (SqlLogFileReader.kt:60-96) caps count (2048), total bytes (8MB) and per-line payload (65536), rejects recursive revisions and verifies a SHA-256 identity before applying, and boundedLines folds over-limit revision lines to the bare prefix (99-118) — sad paths (over-limit, invalid identity, multiple entries per revision) are pinned by O147HistoryUpgradeTest. The main pd line, however, is not revision-prefixed and is therefore subject to the unbounded line buffering of history.reader.unbounded-line-buffering; decode failures fall back to treating the line as a comment (SqlLogFileReader.kt:324-332, SqlLogParamCodec.decode runCatching), which is safe.

surface: User-launched and running JVMs on the developer machine
boundary: Attach authorization: target classification, master switch default-on, consent dialog removed, premain scope

excluded_blocks.block: CLOUD-AND-DEPLOYMENT.md#Workload identity and IAM attack classes
excluded_blocks.reason: No cloud IAM surface in a desktop plugin

local_checks.invariant: Attach only reaches non-helper Java processes from IDE-owned launch surfaces, with a final per-pid re-check that cannot be bypassed by direct pid calls
local_checks.result: Holds for process selection: candidate sources are EXECUTION_TOPIC processStarted handlers and RunContentManager descriptors only (RunConfigurationProcessListener.kt:131-180) — no system-wide pid scan; AgentAttachTarget.classify excludes non-java executables (AgentAttachTarget.kt:81) and the helperClasses deny-list (:151, includes IDEA main, JPS, Gradle/Maven daemons, Kotlin daemon); permitsAttachTarget re-inspects at the final attach entry with readFiles=true so direct attachToPid(pid) calls cannot bypass (AgentManager.kt:464-472, 581-588). Residuals registered in source as accepted: UNKNOWN classification default-allows (AgentManager.kt:470), and test-fork JVMs remain attach candidates via processStarted (RunConfigurationProcessListener.kt:78-79) — both same-principal (user-launched, same account).

local_checks.invariant: Premain injection is scoped to real app runs and authorized by an explicit user decision (consent gate)
local_checks.result: Consent dialog removal is an explicit, documented design decision (PremainInjection.kt:14 'T-EnhancedCaptureDefaultOn: 注入确认闸门已移除'; PluginSettings.kt:637 enhancedCaptureEnabled default true with user-decision KDocs dated 2026-09-16/2026-10-19); the master switch is the declared authorization. Scope gate: PremainTaskScope skips external-system test/IDE task families (PremainTaskScope.kt:94-110) with 'prefer skip over wrong injection' semantics; non-external-system Java configs are always Inject by design (same-principal user-run configs). No cross-principal attach surface found in source.

local_checks.invariant: Attach authorization state (attachedPids idempotency table, premain channel pid) can only be written by the real attached agent
local_checks.result: Fails: onPremainConnected registers attachedPids[pid] (AgentManager.kt:1162) from the self-reported HELLO pid (HELLO_PID_REGEX, AgentManager.kt:157, readHelloPid :1196-1210; pid=0 tolerated and the session is added regardless :1133-1163). A local process that connects to a premain/attach port before the real agent can claim an arbitrary pid; attachToPid's putIfAbsent (AgentManager.kt:585) then skips attaching that pid ('已挂载（幂等表命中），跳过') for as long as the injected session stays healthy (sustained by HEARTBEAT frames within the 30s window), and resumePausedPremainChannelIfHit/resumeAttachPortIfHit key off the same channel.pid. This is the attach-suppression variant of the unauthenticated loopback channel root cause (linked fingerprint agent-ipc-loopback-unauth-session-trust).

hunter_hardening: AgentProtocol.escapeArrayItem (AgentProtocol.kt:121-124) escapes only backslash, quote, and \b\f\n\r\t; other control characters (<0x20 except those, and 0x7F) pass unescaped. The agent-side hand-rolled extractor (SenderLoop.extractStringArray:504-543) treats them literally so no structural injection results today, but the decode is asymmetric — IDE-escaped '\n' arrives as backslash+n and is decoded to a bare letter 'n', mangling skip prefixes that contain control characters; a shared strict JSON encoder/decoder on both sides would remove the drift.

AgentSession read loop (AgentSessionSupport.kt:457-461) treats a negative frame length as 'continue' without consuming bytes, permanently desyncing the stream and emitting one WARN per 4 garbage bytes — an accepted local peer can flood idea.log indefinitely; cap desync warnings and close the session.

SenderLoop MAX_FAST_DROPS=10 (SenderLoop.java:112, :322-337) lets a local process force the agent to permanently abandon its port with 10 accept-then-close connections, silently ending capture for that run with only a stderr line inside the app JVM and no IDE-side signal.

surface: Any local process able to open a TCP connection to the loopback agent ports
boundary: Loopback channel boundary: no peer authentication; connection -> event/config authority over IDE and agent
selected_companion_blocks: DESKTOP-MOBILE-AND-LOCAL-IPC.md#Local IPC and exported-component attack classes

local_checks.invariant: The agent listening sockets restrict network exposure to loopback and authenticate the connecting peer before granting session authority
local_checks.result: Loopback binding holds (ServerSocket(0,1,InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()) AgentManager.kt:799; premain :899; re-bind :1577-1581), but peer authentication is entirely absent: accept() results become AgentSession objects with no OS peer credential, token, or channel-ownership check anywhere on the accept path (attachAndOffer :824-833, acceptPremain :993-1046, onPremainConnected :1112-1188). Session identity is the self-reported HELLO pid (AgentManager.kt:157, :1196-1210); pid=0 is accepted and a session is still committed (AgentSessionSupport.kt:1133-1163). Any local process that discovers the ephemeral port is granted full session authority.

local_checks.invariant: EVENT and CONFIG_ACK frames are only honored from the verified agent peer, and frame-level gates check identity rather than only capture state
local_checks.result: Fails: AgentSession.handleFrame (AgentSessionSupport.kt:486-588) accepts EVENT/HEARTBEAT/CONFIG_ACK from any connected socket; the only pre-sink gates are listenActiveProvider (:513-522) and userPaused (:538-547) — neither verifies the peer. CMD_CONFIG_ACK sets configAckDisabled (AgentSessionSupport.kt:576) which is the sole truth source for captureConfirmedActive (AgentManager.kt:1351) driving SqlCaptureGate.paused (AgentManager.kt:1283-1284): an injected peer can flip the bridge gate (suppress console capture) or fabricate 'agent confirmed active' state. A spoofed HELLO pid also poisons attachedPids (AgentManager.kt:1162) to suppress future attach of chosen pids (:585).

local_checks.invariant: The agent-side sender authenticates the endpoint it writes SQL frames (with literal parameter values) to, and only accepts control input from the IDE
local_checks.result: Fails: SenderLoop.run dials 127.0.0.1:serverPort unconditionally (SenderLoop.java:225) and writes HELLO, HEARTBEAT, and EVENT frames (SQL text + literal parameter values, :237-239, :261-271) to whatever answers the port; inbound CONFIG from that same peer is applied via the contains-parser (:429-471). A local process that wins the port (ephemeral race, or binding after the IDE channel closes while the agent retries with 1s-5s backoff, :315-348) receives the frames and can defeat the 15s no-CONFIG watchdog (:295-303) by sending {"disabled":false}, keeping the exfiltration stream alive indefinitely. MAX_FAST_DROPS=10 (:112, :322-337) additionally lets a local process force the agent to permanently abandon its port (silent capture loss for the run).

surface: Frames on the custom length-prefixed TCP protocol between IDE and agent
boundary: Protocol parsing boundary: frame length, HELLO pid parsing, CONFIG body application, skip-prefix strings
selected_companion_blocks: PROTOCOLS-RPC-AND-MESSAGING.md#Framing, schema, and interpretation attack classes

local_checks.invariant: Frame length is bounded on both directions and cannot drive oversized allocation or unbounded reads
local_checks.result: Holds: both sides cap payload at MAX_FRAME_LEN=1MB (AgentProtocol.kt:41, SenderLoop.java:53). IDE read loop rejects len<0/>1MB and skipNBytes-drops oversized bodies without killing the session (AgentSessionSupport.kt:456-461); agent-side readInboundFrame rejects len<=0/>1MB by throwing a non-timeout IOException into the reconnect path (SenderLoop.java:570-608) with partial-frame detection distinguishing idle from desync.

local_checks.invariant: HELLO pid extraction and CONFIG_ACK parsing cannot be confused by crafted bodies (no delimiter/regex injection)
local_checks.result: Holds at the parsing layer: HELLO_PID_REGEX (AgentManager.kt:157) captures digits only and toLongOrNull-guards (:1205-1206) — no injection into the Long pid; CMD_CONFIG_ACK is parsed by a strict matchEntire regex with fixed key order and bounded value domain (AgentProtocol.kt:159-187), malformed bodies counted and dropped. (The pid being attacker-chosen is an identity problem owned by the agent-ipc unit, not a parse-injection.)

local_checks.invariant: Skip-prefix/biz-prefix values in CONFIG bodies cannot break out of the string array or spoof the contains-based boolean keys on the agent side
local_checks.result: Holds: escapeArrayItem escapes backslash, double quote, and \b\f\n\r\t (AgentProtocol.kt:121-124); the agent-side hand-rolled extractStringArray handles backslash escapes and quote boundaries symmetrically for those characters (SenderLoop.java:504-543), and the contains-based boolean keys ("disabled":true / "desensitize":false, :429-437) cannot appear unescaped inside an array item because the quote is always escaped — verified by constructing the escaped form of a prefix containing those substrings. stackFrames digits are scanned then clamped to 12..64 agent-side (SenderLoop.java:455-471, AgentState.java:89-92). Remaining weaknesses are hardening (control-char escape asymmetry), not boundary failures.

surface: Any local process able to open a TCP connection to the loopback agent ports
boundary: Spoofed/spurious agent events flow into the same downstream sinks as console lines (panel, autosave, jump-to-source)

local_checks.invariant: Every attacker-influenceable EVENT field that reaches a navigation or file sink is enumerated and bounded
local_checks.result: Field map established: AgentEvent.parse (AgentEvent.kt:43-79) accepts sf (sourceFile), sl (sourceLine), cands (file/line/class triples), mk, rt, sd, th, url, sql, p — all fully attacker-chosen for an injected frame; AgentEventAdapter.toEntry (AgentEventAdapter.kt:36-73) copies sourceFile/sourceLine/sourceCandidates/candidateClasses/stackDigest/threadName and derives databaseName/dialectName from url into LogSqlEntry with no validation.

local_checks.invariant: Spoofed sourceFile/sourceCandidates can only navigate within project-declared roots (no traversal or arbitrary-file open)
local_checks.result: Navigation sink is EntryJumpResolver.resolve (:33-48) -> SourcePathResolver.resolveVirtualFile (EntrySourceMatcher.kt:94-114), which only concatenates the (trimmed, backslash-normalized) relative path under project basePath, module content roots, and source roots and calls LocalFileSystem.findFileByPath — no direct absolute-path acceptance in source and read-only editor navigation only. Residual not source-decidable: whether findFileByPath normalizes '..' segments (VFS paths are typically canonical, but this is platform behavior, not repo source); impact is bounded to editor navigation (deception), not file writes.

local_checks.invariant: Fields written into autosave files cannot forge additional protocol lines
local_checks.result: Fails at the write layer: SqlLogAutoSaver.writeEntryText writes entry.sourceFile verbatim into the '-- source: ' header (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:488-490) with no newline/control-char sanitization, so a spoofed EVENT sf value containing newlines forges arbitrary additional header/pd lines in the autosaved file that SqlLogFileReader re-imports. No capability gain beyond direct event injection (the whole entry, including restoredSql, is attacker-chosen and autosaved anyway), so this is a variant of the same channel root cause, not an independent root cause.

local_checks.invariant: The connection URL used as dialect-inference evidence comes from the real agent session only
local_checks.result: Fails: a spoofed EVENT url field is remembered per session (AgentSessionSupport.kt:499-503) and pushed into AgentUrlRegistry via onUrlCaptured/syncInferenceUrl (AgentManager.kt:432-434, 757), where the inference layer treats it as the agent-observed connection URL (also invalidating DataSourceUrlProbe, AgentManager.kt:443-446) — corrupts dialect rendering namespace and datasource dialect evidence. Same root cause.

surface: AI agents connected through the platform MCP server
boundary: File-read confinement: project-root containment, traversal, drive letters, symlink canonicalization

local_checks.invariant: Agent-supplied filePath cannot escape the project root via traversal, UNC, drive-relative, ADS, or absolute-outside forms
local_checks.result: resolveInsideProject (McpFilePathResolver.kt:41-55) unifies backslashes then rejects any substring '..' and any '//'-prefixed path (covers UNC and \\?\ device forms); WINDOWS_DRIVE regex makes 'C:x' drive-relative forms take the absolute branch, which requires the exact case-sensitive '$base/' prefix so any outside or case-mismatched absolute path fails closed; the relative branch re-runs McpRenderInput.normalizeFilePath (:75-79: trim, backslash unification, leading-slash strip, reject '..' and drive letters) so a leading '/' cannot become an absolute escape. NTFS ADS syntax ('file.xml:ads') cannot parse as java.nio WindowsPath (second colon) and toRealPath failure is caught fail-closed in canonicalProjectFile (:58-63); device names fail the Files.isRegularFile check. Existing McpFilePathResolverTest cases corroborate (UNC rejection, out-of-project rejection, dot-dot rejection, symlink-out rejection).

local_checks.invariant: All file-reading MCP tools route through the resolver (no bypass path) and symlinks are canonicalized before read
local_checks.result: Every file-reading tool in scope resolves via McpFilePathResolver.resolveFile: render_sql (McpSourceLocator.renderAtLine:69), mapper_check (SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:57), crud_sql (SqlVisualizerCrudSqlTool.kt:115). canonicalProjectFile calls toRealPath on both root and target and requires target.startsWith(root) plus a regular file, so an in-project symlink pointing outside is rejected before findFileByPath (:58-70). No raw LocalFileSystem/PsiManager lookup of agent paths found in these files.

local_checks.invariant: No exploitable TOCTOU between symlink canonicalization and file read crossing the project boundary
local_checks.result: Source shows a check/use window: toRealPath canonicalization (McpFilePathResolver.kt:58-63) and the subsequent read (SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:57-58 via VirtualFile.inputStream) are not atomic, so a concurrent local process swapping the path to a symlink could redirect a read. However the only principal able to modify the project directory is a local process that already holds developer-equivalent filesystem authority, so no boundary is crossed and no privilege is gained; recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: The user-customizable history directory (absolute path outside project) must not become an agent-controlled traversal sink
local_checks.result: resolveHistoryDir (SqlVisualizerHistorySearchTool.kt:127-132) uses the operator-set application-level logAutoSavePath verbatim, with the same basePath-or-user.home fallback as the writer SqlLogAutoSaver.resolveDir (SqlLogAutoSaver.kt:613-628) — exact read/write parity, single source. The agent cannot influence the directory (no MCP tool writes settings); the search only reads files with a .sql extension inside that one directory (HistorySearchService.kt:135-139). The user.home fallback (:130) mirrors the writer's fallback, so it reads only where the plugin itself writes.

hunter_hardening: McpToolGate.isEnabled is fail-open (runCatching getOrDefault(true), McpToolGate.kt:46-49): if the PluginSettings application service is unavailable the gate opens; a fail-closed fallback would match the deny-by-default intent, though in a normal IDE run the service is always registered.

Filter-EP degrade-open (McpGateFilterRegistrar UNKNOWN contract or McpGateFilterEpBridge reflection failure) leaves disabled sqlv_* tools visible in the external session tool listing; invocation remains denied by the audit-time check, so the exposure is limited to tool names/descriptions of tools the operator disabled.

TOCTOU window between McpFilePathResolver.canonicalProjectFile toRealPath and the later VirtualFile read (e.g. SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:57): re-verifying the canonical target at open time (or reading via the canonical Path with a no-follow open) would close the symlink-swap window against concurrent local processes.

McpFilePathResolver.resolveInsideProject rejects any path containing '..' even as a legitimate filename component (e.g. 'data..2024.xml'), an over-strict fail-closed behavior; harmless security-wise but worth noting to avoid future loosening pressure.

sqlv_render_logs accepts logText with no total input cap (per-statement 20k cap only, MyBatisLogParser.maxParseLength); a platform-channel size bound is the only de facto limit — an explicit total cap would mirror the McpRenderInput snippet cap.

McpAuditLog args summaries (e.g. executionArgsSummary with selectSql for sqlv_explain) write truncated agent SQL text into idea.log; local-only, but consistent masking with mcpMaskEnabled would align the audit channel with the output-masking intent.

McpAuditLog args summaries (e.g. executionArgsSummary with selectSql for sqlv_explain) write truncated agent SQL text into idea.log; local-only, but consistent masking with mcpMaskEnabled would align the audit channel with the output-masking intent.

surface: AI agents connected through the platform MCP server (untrusted tool arguments reaching JDBC)
boundary: Read-only execution guard: single-SELECT structural check, literal stripping, keyword sweep, fail-closed parsing

local_checks.invariant: checkSingleSelect fail-closed gate order: null/blank -> 200k length cap -> parse via SqlAstParser single entry (allowSquareBracketQuotation only) -> exactly one statement -> Statement is Select -> FOR UPDATE/SHARE via forUpdateTable+forMode -> INTO via intoTables/intoTempTable -> keyword sweep on literal-stripped lowercase text -> phrase sweep; parse failure (catch Throwable, incl. StackOverflowError) denies with SQL_BLOCKED
local_checks.result: Order and failure semantics verified at McpSelectGuard.kt:73-128; SqlAstParser.parseStatements converts the JSqlParser 5.3 silent-null simple-parse result into JSQLParserException (SqlAstParser.kt:36-41) so null parses also fail closed; multi-statement gate at :100-105 counts Statements including empty-statement forms.

local_checks.invariant: Literal-stripper quote-model divergence cannot hide an engine-visible keyword from the deny sweep
local_checks.result: stripLiterals (McpSelectGuard.kt:136-177) masks '...', "...", `...`, [...] and strips --/;; all observed mismatches fail in the deny direction: MySQL backslash-escaped quotes and Postgres U&'' escapes make the stripper close early, leaving tail text visible to the sweep (false positives only); Postgres $$-quoted strings are not masked at all so their content stays visible and any contained verb is swept; SQL Server ]] bracket escaping over-closes the bracket mask leaving text visible; unterminated quotes hide only text JSqlParser would reject at parse (fail-closed earlier). No route found where masked text hides a keyword the engine would execute.

local_checks.invariant: No non-SELECT slips into the execute() multi-result tolerant channel: that channel is reachable only with channelNote != null, and the executed text is a plugin-constant wrapper around the guard-validated selectSql
local_checks.result: McpDbExecutor.kt:324-330 picks executeQuery(String) when channelNote==null and executeStatementCollectFirst (:394-411, bounded MAX_RESULT_HOPS=32) otherwise. On the MCP chain channelNote is non-null only for Oracle (EXPLAIN PLAN FOR {sql}) and SQL Server (SET STATISTICS XML ON; {sql}; SET STATISTICS XML OFF) — constant templates in ExplainSupport.kt:131-176 with literal {sql} replacement (:198); {sql} is the guard-validated selectSql trimmed with a single removeSuffix(";") (SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:131), which cannot introduce a new statement since the multi-statement gate already ran on the raw text and the wrapper only appends constants. grep confirms no executeUpdate and no other execute( path in the mcp package. Agent-controlled dialect parameter can only mis-select these constant wrappers (engine syntax errors), not inject statements.

local_checks.invariant: askPassword=false fail-closed on the MCP channel (zero-popup, no modal password prompt): no default value, MCP call site must pass false explicitly
local_checks.result: executeQuery has askPassword as a required parameter without default (McpDbExecutor.kt:206-215); setAskPassword is invoked unconditionally at :295-296; the MCP call site passes askPassword=false (SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:158), so an unsaved password surfaces as a connection failure instead of a modal prompt.

local_checks.invariant: Row budget is clamped at both tool layer and channel layer; nothing the agent passes can exceed HARD_MAX_ROWS
local_checks.result: McpExplainFormatter.clampMaxRows (:56-58) maps null/<=0 to DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS=200 and >1000 to HARD_MAX_ROWS=1000; the tool clamps before building the target (SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:43) and the channel re-clamps via channelRowBudget before collection (McpDbExecutor.kt:44, :286, collect stops at maxRows :429-432).

local_checks.invariant: setQueryTimeout guard: driver-level timeout applied before execution for timeoutSeconds>0
local_checks.result: McpDbExecutor.kt:311-316 sets the timeout best-effort: a reflection failure is logged ("guard off") and execution proceeds with NO timeout; the MCP chain passes PluginSettings.executionTimeoutSeconds whose default is 30s (ExecutionTimeoutGuard.DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) but 0 disables it entirely; Statement.cancel on timeout-like exceptions (:339-349) only fires when a timeout was set. Row budget bounds rows, not query cost/duration. Hardening, not a candidate: the setting is operator-owned and the timeout is a suggestion the driver may ignore.

local_checks.invariant: Second gate after the guard: first keyword must be SELECT/VALUES/TABLE/WITH with full word boundaries (SELECTED/SELECT_foo rejected), comments and leading parens skipped
local_checks.result: ExplainGate.isExplainableSource (ExplainGate.kt:85-86) applied at SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:81-88 after the structural guard; both gates align on VALUES (1) and TABLE users (Select subclasses in JSqlParser 5.3, pinned by McpSelectGuardTest `放行_可 EXPLAIN 的非 SELECT 形态`); `TABLE t FOR UPDATE` would still be denied by the guard's forMode field and the "for update" phrase sweep regardless of parse shape.

local_checks.invariant: Keyword sweep completeness: function-form exemptions (insert/truncate) cannot open a write path, and case/comment/terminator obfuscation variants are denied
local_checks.result: SCALAR_FUNCTION_FORM_WORDS={insert,truncate} (McpSelectGuard.kt:61) exempts only `word<optional ws>(` (isScalarFunctionForm :197-201); any other occurrence denies, and real write statements never reach the sweep because the structural gate requires a parsed single Select (comment :57-59 — verified sound). Keyword splitting via comments cannot help an attacker: comments are stripped so the surrounding verbs remain visible, and any write-bearing text must independently parse as a single Select which JSqlParser 5.3 rejects (WITH...INSERT parses as Insert statement -> !is Select; data-modifying CTEs are not a JSqlParser production). McpSelectGuardTest pins the deny matrix plus the bracket-quotation negative samples added with the SqlAstParser consolidation.

local_checks.invariant: MAX_SQL_LENGTH=200_000 gate position: length cap applied to trimmed input before any parser work
local_checks.result: Verified McpSelectGuard.kt:24, :77-83 — cap runs after trim, before parseStatements, so oversized input cannot reach JSqlParser; test `拒绝_超长输入` pins the boundary.

local_checks.invariant: hasIntoClause recursiveness: INTO detection must cover CTE (WithItem) bodies and derived-table/join subselects, not only the top-level PlainSelect and direct SetOperationList branches
local_checks.result: Gap found: hasIntoClause (McpSelectGuard.kt:216-222) inspects only the top-level PlainSelect and SetOperationList direct branches; a PlainSelect nested as a CTE body or derived table is never visited. The comment at :215 claims CTE INTO still lands on PlainSelect, but only the outermost PlainSelect is checked. The phrase sweep backstop (FORBIDDEN_PHRASES :64-67) covers only into outfile/dumpfile/var/@ — plain `SELECT ... INTO tbl` inside a CTE escapes both layers. Nested FOR UPDATE is NOT affected (the "for update"/"for share"/"lock in share mode" phrases are substring-swept anywhere in the text). Candidate recorded as needs_validation: whether JSqlParser 5.3 parses CTE-embedded INTO with intoTables on the inner PlainSelect, and whether any supported engine executes it, is not source-visible.

local_checks.invariant: The read-only guarantee is enforced at the database layer, not only by client-side text analysis: connection/session placed in a read-only mode before executing on any project datasource
local_checks.result: No DB-layer read-only enforcement exists: grep of src/main shows zero uses of connection.setReadOnly, SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, or session read-only initialization anywhere on the executor chain. McpDbExecutor builds a DatabaseConnectionManager connection with the datasource's stored credentials (:287-302) and executes with only a best-effort setQueryTimeout (:311-316). The guard is purely a statement-shape/keyword filter, so any statement that parses as a single plain SELECT but carries server-side effects through SELECT-invoked functions/stored routines (e.g. PG functions performing DML, MySQL stored functions, load_file(), pg_read_file, lo_import, dblink, pg_sleep) or planner-time evaluation executes with the datasource account's full privileges, while the tool advertises readOnlyHint=TRUE and "Strictly read-only" (SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:18-33). Candidate recorded as needs_validation: the decisive facts (engine-side function execution under the configured account, behavior over the DBN RemoteStatement mirror) are not source-visible.

hunter_hardening: setQueryTimeout is best-effort: on reflection failure the executor logs 'guard off' and proceeds with no timeout (McpDbExecutor.kt:311-316), and setting executionTimeoutSeconds=0 disables it entirely; the row budget bounds rows but not query cost/duration, so expensive cartesian joins or pg_sleep-style SELECTs from the MCP channel are bounded only by the driver honoring the suggestion.

SQL Server wrapper trailing terminator can be swallowed: `selectSql` ending in a `--` line comment (e.g. `SELECT 1 --`) survives the guard, and the rendered batch `SET STATISTICS XML ON; SELECT 1 --; SET STATISTICS XML OFF` leaves STATISTICS XML ON on the (possibly pooled) connection, polluting subsequent statements' results on that session; consider stripping trailing comments before wrapping or re-validating the rendered statement.

stripLiterals does not model SQL Server ]] bracket escaping, MySQL NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, or Postgres dollar-quoting; all observed mismatches fail toward over-blocking (false positives), never toward hiding engine-visible keywords — worth a comment to keep future edits from reversing that direction.

FORBIDDEN_WORDS intentionally omits desc/replace/comment, relying on the structural `is Select` gate; correct today because JSqlParser 5.3's Select family (PlainSelect, SetOperationList, Values, TableStatement) contains no write form, but any future loosening of the structural gate makes the sweep incomplete by design — the ExplainGate second gate at SqlVisualizerExplainTool.kt:81 is a useful third layer to preserve.

MAX_RESULT_HOPS=32 bounds the execute() result walk (McpDbExecutor.kt:402-408), but result sets beyond the first are never drained; statement.close in the finally block covers the JDBC side, so this is only a driver-behavior cleanliness note.
