surface: AI agents connected through the platform MCP server
boundary: Tool authority boundary: master switch, per-tool disable, filter-EP degrade-open, session visibility

local_checks.invariant: Every sqlv_* tool invocation is denied when the master switch is off or the tool is in the per-tool disable list, regardless of listing visibility
local_checks.result: Invocation-time enforcement is universal and independent of the filter EP: McpToolsetSupport.audit (McpToolsetSupport.kt:142-144) checks McpToolGate.isEnabled(tool) before each tool body and throws TOOL_DISABLED; all 11 @McpTool methods (grep of SqlVisualizer*.kt) wrap their bodies in audit() with their correct tool name. isEnabled re-reads PluginSettings state on every call (McpToolGate.kt:46-49), so master-switch and per-tool revocation take effect at the next call without IDE restart.

local_checks.invariant: Degrade-open of the mcpToolFilterProvider EP (unrecognized contract or registration failure) must not grant invocation authority for disabled tools
local_checks.result: Degrade-open is visibility-only, not authority-bearing. On UNKNOWN contract McpGateFilterEpRegistrar skips registration (McpGateFilterRegistrar.kt:56-64); bridge failures degrade to empty filter list / unchanged context (McpGateFilterEpBridge.kt:124-132, 172-193). In all degrade states a disabled tool at worst remains listed; calling it still hits the audit-time isEnabled check and is rejected. getUpdates returns emptyFlow so the platform recomputes the filter chain per listing (McpGateFilterEpBridge.kt:32-33, 84-85), giving revocation-without-restart on the listing path too.

local_checks.invariant: Runtime-generated shell classes (TinyClassFileWriter + ShellClassLoader.defineClass) must not create an injection path into class definition
local_checks.result: No agent-reachable input: shellBytes is generated solely from TOOL_CLASSES constants and the platform McpToolset interface name (McpToolsetDynamicRegistrar.kt:96-130); the hand-written bytecode is a fixed minimal template (TinyClassFileWriter.shellBytes) with no attacker-influenced bytes; ShellClassLoader.define is internal and invoked only from registerToolset. Defined-class and EP-registration ledgers prevent duplicate define/register (McpToolsetDynamicRegistrar.kt:56-60, 105-117).

hunter_hardening: McpToolGate.isEnabled is fail-open (runCatching getOrDefault(true), McpToolGate.kt:46-49): if the PluginSettings application service is unavailable the gate opens; a fail-closed fallback would match the deny-by-default intent, though in a normal IDE run the service is always registered.

Filter-EP degrade-open (McpGateFilterRegistrar UNKNOWN contract or McpGateFilterEpBridge reflection failure) leaves disabled sqlv_* tools visible in the external session tool listing; invocation remains denied by the audit-time check, so the exposure is limited to tool names/descriptions of tools the operator disabled.

TOCTOU window between McpFilePathResolver.canonicalProjectFile toRealPath and the later VirtualFile read (e.g. SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:57): re-verifying the canonical target at open time (or reading via the canonical Path with a no-follow open) would close the symlink-swap window against concurrent local processes.

surface: AI agents connected through the platform MCP server: raw agent-supplied SQL strings accepted by the four text-analysis tools sqlv_check_sql, sqlv_rollback_plan, sqlv_reverse_sql, sqlv_perf_advice
boundary: Bounded-evaluation boundary: agent-controlled SQL text parsed by JSqlParser/SqlAstParser and rollback/reverse pipelines with no input-length cap or parse-cost bound on these entry points

local_checks.invariant: Agent-supplied SQL text entering the JSqlParser/SqlAstParser sink is length-capped at the MCP entry points, matching the 20k maxParseLength invariant the render-logs path enforces for the same sink class
local_checks.result: No cap exists on any of the four entry points: sqlv_check_sql(sql: String) at SqlVisualizerCheckSqlTool.kt:39, sqlv_rollback_plan(sql: String) at SqlVisualizerRollbackPlanTool.kt:37-40, sqlv_reverse_sql(sql: String) at SqlVisualizerReverseSqlTool.kt:44-48, sqlv_perf_advice(sql: String) at SqlVisualizerPerfAdviceTool.kt:56-57, and SqlAstParser.parseStatements/parseSingle (SqlAstParser.kt:36-49) impose no length or cost bound before CCJSqlParserUtil. The sibling control is source-visible and real: all four console log parsers and the MCP render-logs tool enforce PluginSettings.DEFAULT_LOG_MAX_PARSE_LENGTH=20000 (PluginSettings.kt:832; SqlVisualizerRenderLogsTool.kt:82) for the same SQL-text-to-JSqlParser sink class. RollbackSqlGenerator bounds are output-only (MAX_STATEMENTS=500 line 101, MAX_TOTAL_CHARS=256KiB line 104) and do not bound parse input.

local_checks.invariant: Tool-side error handling contains parser failures so an unbounded parse cannot produce a fatal path in the IDE process
local_checks.result: Partial containment only, and asymmetric: UnboundedWriteDetector.detect catches Exception (line 162) and RollbackSqlGenerator.generate catches Exception (line 133), so a JVM-level StackOverflowError/OutOfMemoryError from JSqlParser propagates; SqlPerfAnalyzer.analyze wraps parseSingle in runCatching (line 122) which catches Throwable. The MCP audit boundary (McpToolsetSupport.kt:146-147) deliberately rethrows VirtualMachineError per FatalErrors.isFatal (VirtualMachineError/LinkageError/ThreadDeath), so a parser StackOverflowError escapes the plugin to the platform MCP dispatcher. Dispatcher-side containment is IntelliJ platform behavior not visible in this repository.

local_checks.invariant: SqlReverseParser has bounded recursion depth and non-infinite loops on agent-supplied input
local_checks.result: Loops advance the cursor or throw on each iteration (spot-checked parseTailClauses 292-326, parseAndSegment 801-815, parseIn 1077-1091), so no non-advancing loop was found. Recursion is unbounded: the parenthesized-condition branch (parseConditionInternal 859-866) recurses parseGroup (962-963) -> parseConditionList (782) -> parseAndSegment (801) -> parseCondition (842) -> parseConditionInternal (856), roughly 4-5 stack frames per nesting level with no depth counter anywhere in the file (no depth/limit guard found by grep); a secondary cycle parseSubqueryTable (679) -> parseSubqueryStructure (707) -> parse (34) recurses per FROM-subquery nesting level. The tool catches only SqlReverseException (SqlVisualizerReverseSqlTool.kt:55-65), so StackOverflowError propagates to the fatal-passthrough audit boundary.

local_checks.invariant: Output-side budgets in the rollback/perf pipelines bound the tool response regardless of input
local_checks.result: RollbackSqlGenerator.enforceLimits (595-603) caps statements at 500 / 256KiB total; perf advice caps findings at MAX_FINDINGS=30 and message cells at 200 chars (SqlVisualizerPerfAdviceTool.kt:31,39,94-121); check_sql output grows one line per statement (proportional to input). These are output-only bounds: none of them bounds input parse cost or AST memory, which is the gap recorded in the candidates.

hunter_hardening: sqlv_schema_context alias-miss error enumerates every configured datasource display name to the agent (McpSchemaContextService.kt:94-101) before any table-level check; capping the list or gating it behind a successful authz-equivalent step would reduce blind enumeration value

unaliased sqlv_schema_context yields a table-existence oracle across all project datasources (hit vs 'no schema metadata for X', outcomeOf 143-154); S3 source disclosure mitigates wrong-source reads but not enumeration — an explicit multi-source opt-in flag or per-call datasource cap would scope it

error-handling asymmetry between sibling channels: perf_advice wraps JSqlParser in runCatching (SqlPerfAnalyzer.kt:122, catches Throwable) while check_sql and rollback_plan catch only Exception (UnboundedWriteDetector.kt:162, RollbackSqlGenerator.kt:133) — unifying on fatal-passthrough semantics with an input cap would make the four channels consistent

schema context output has a per-cell 200-char cap but no per-table column cap (McpSchemaFormatter.format emits every column of each returned table), so very wide tables dominate output; a per-table column budget would bound it

UnboundedWriteDetector.parseStatementsShared single AST slot is @Volatile and shared between the UI EDT confirm flow and the MCP dispatcher thread; content-equality check before reuse prevents wrong-AST reuse today, but any future consumer that mutates nodes would need to leave the shared slot first (existing hard constraint documented at UnboundedWriteDetector.kt:79-82)

surface: AI agents connected through the platform MCP server; captured SQL history with literal parameter values
boundary: Data-exposure boundary: history search/render tools expose captured SQL and parameter values to connected agents

local_checks.invariant: Result scoping and budgets on the history-exposure channel (default today-scope, result caps, preview truncation, scan cap)
local_checks.result: Scoping controls are present and enforced: default scope is today's entries (HistorySearchService.kt:239-245, allDates required to widen), maxResults clamped to 1..100 (:228, :48-51), per-hit SQL preview capped at 8 lines/600 chars (:327-337), scan capped at 200_000 entries with scanTruncated flag (:60, :146-162). Exposure of captured SQL with literal parameter values to connected agents is the tool's declared feature gated by the master switch; allDates full-history exposure is operator-accepted tool semantics, not an invariant failure by itself.

local_checks.invariant: The 'MCP output masking' setting (mcpMaskEnabled) keeps sensitive literals out of the AI context on every MCP output channel carrying restored SQL
local_checks.result: Masking is applied on exactly one channel: SqlVisualizerRenderLogsTool.renderLogs applies DisplayMasker.maskDisplay(entry.restoredSql, maskOn) when mcpMaskEnabled is on (SqlVisualizerRenderLogsTool.kt:99-112; RenderLogsToolTest asserts masked/unmasked behavior). The sibling channel serving the same data class — sqlv_history_search — returns preview(e.restoredSql) with parameters back-filled as literal values and never calls DisplayMasker (SqlVisualizerHistorySearchTool.formatResult:107-121; HistorySearchService.buildResult:267-280). A user who enables masking to keep production literals out of the AI context still leaks them through history_search. See candidate mcp.history_search.masking-not-applied.

local_checks.invariant: Agent-supplied regex over history text must have bounded evaluation cost
local_checks.result: No regex budget exists: the agent's regex is compiled with only a syntax check (HistorySearchService.kt:230-234, Regex(pattern, IGNORE_CASE)) and evaluated with containsMatchIn per entry over rawSql/restoredSql (:221) on the MCP dispatcher thread inside the IDE process. The 200_000-entry scan cap bounds entry count but not per-regex cost; per-entry SQL can reach the 20k maxParseLength. Catastrophic-backtracking patterns are unthrottled (no timeout/step budget), and adversarial long tokens can be planted into history by the agent itself via sqlv_explain selectSql recorded through mcpHistoryEntry (McpToolsetSupport.kt:302-320) into the autosave chain. local_checks.invariant: Agent-supplied XML snippets and mapper XML file content entering the parse/render pipeline are length-bounded and parsed with hardened XML features
local_checks.result: Snippet form is bounded (MAX_SNIPPET_LENGTH=100_000) and sourceType whitelisted to xml_mapper (McpRenderInput.kt:16-19, 49-65); file form is confined by McpFilePathResolver (see unit 2). Both reach XmlMapperParser, whose single XML parse entry point is SecureXml.parse (XmlMapperParser.kt:191) — XXE features off plus inline-DTD expansion pre-scan per the platform-wide hardened parser. Render output is analysis text only; mapper_check has no execution or write sink.

local_checks.invariant: Agent-supplied log text injected into the parser chain cannot reach a sink beyond text returned to the calling agent, and per-statement cost is bounded
local_checks.result: renderLogs feeds logText line-wise through four parsers whose per-statement length is capped at maxParseLength (20k default; MyBatisLogParser.kt:87,152,186,270); output is restored-SQL text appended to the response for the calling agent only. No persistence into history (mcpHistoryEntry is not called from this tool), no audit-log SQL echo (argsSummary stays the literal 'ok', McpToolsetSupport.kt:235), no execution sink. Note for hardening: logText itself has no total input cap; the bound is the per-statement cap and whatever the platform MCP channel imposes (not source-visible).

local_checks.invariant: Agent-chosen mapper/entity file selection is read-only and confined to project scope
local_checks.result: sqlv_render_sql locates via McpFilePathResolver.resolveFile inside ReadAction (McpSourceLocator.kt:67-99); sqlv_crud_sql resolves filePath through the same resolver or className via JavaPsiFacade within project-scoped PSI search (SqlVisualizerCrudSqlTool.kt:63-78, 114-122). All paths are PSI-read-only; the CRUD chain generates SQL text and never executes.

boundary: Data-exposure boundary: agent-controlled table-name enumeration returns schema metadata plus datasource display names and target database; unaliased calls scan every configured datasource

local_checks.invariant: Only schema metadata (table/column names, types, comments, NOT NULL) and datasource display names reach agent output; no credentials or JDBC URL fragments are emitted, so the KDoc claim 'credentials never leave the IDE' holds for every emitted field
local_checks.result: McpSchemaFormatter.format (lines 72-94) emits only table name, table comment, column name, typeSpec, column comment and NOT NULL marks, each cell truncated at MAX_CELL_CHARS=200 (line 18, cell() 162-163). The JDBC URL obtained via RawConnectionConfig.getUrl() reflection (McpSchemaContextService.targetDatabase, lines 345-352) is consumed only by JdbcUrlDatabase.nameFromUrl to derive the target database name and is never serialized into the Outcome text; no password field is read anywhere in the service. Emitted datasource identity is limited to DasDataSource.getName() display names (dsName, lines 363-369). The KDoc claim holds for every emitted field.

local_checks.invariant: Agent-controlled tables whitelist and maxTables bound per-call enumeration (1-50 names, maxTables clamped to 20)
local_checks.result: parseTableNames (lines 113-117) rejects non-string JSON shapes and delegates to sanitizeTableNames (49-59) which rejects empty and >MAX_TABLE_NAMES=50 (line 21) lists with case-insensitive dedupe; parseMaxTables (147-148) result is clamped by clampMaxTables (39-43) to default 8 / hard max 20; requested>shown produces a truncation hint (format, lines 87-92). Per-call table-name enumeration is bounded as documented.

local_checks.invariant: Whether the whitelist bounds cross-source enumeration: unaliased calls must not silently scan or leak schema across every configured datasource
local_checks.result: With alias omitted, targetSources (lines 119-123) returns every configured datasource (findDataSource(project, null) returns singleOrNull; multi-source case maps all names), and collectEntries (177-206) resolves each requested table first-hit across all sources. This is documented deliberate one-期 parity ('无别名即全扫', lines 115-118) and the cross-source auto-resolve incidents are mitigated by S3 disclosure: output prefixes 'source: <names> (auto-resolved; pass dataSource to pin one)' (lines 159-166). Residual effect: an existence oracle across all project datasources via hit-vs-'no schema metadata for X' (outcomeOf, 143-154), and the alias-miss error enumerates all datasource display names (94-101). Alias is optional, so the whitelist bounds table names per call but not datasource scope; because the tool's declared purpose is read-only metadata of operator-configured datasources and source disclosure is present, this is recorded as hardening rather than a boundary failure. Alias present and matching scopes the scan to that single datasource (P4, line 120).

local_checks.invariant: Per-call scan cost is bounded and repeat cost is capped (cross-call index discipline)
local_checks.result: Each datasource's DasModel is fully traversed via reflection at most once per call (scanSource, 223-239) and cached cross-call under a WeakHashMap identity key with 30s TTL (INDEX_TTL_MS, line 267), 64-entry fail-safe clear (INDEX_CACHE_MAX, line 273), targetDb re-validation (cachedIndex, 301-308) and DDL invalidation via MetadataInvalidator registration (284-290). Scan cost scales with operator-configured introspection model size, not with agent input; namespace ancestor walk is bounded at MAX_ANCESTOR_DEPTH=4 (line 51, 446-463). No agent-driven amplification path found.

hunter_hardening: sqlv_schema_context alias-miss error enumerates every configured datasource display name to the agent (McpSchemaContextService.kt:94-101) before any table-level check; capping the list or gating it behind a successful authz-equivalent step would reduce blind enumeration value

unaliased sqlv_schema_context yields a table-existence oracle across all project datasources (hit vs 'no schema metadata for X', outcomeOf 143-154); S3 source disclosure mitigates wrong-source reads but not enumeration — an explicit multi-source opt-in flag or per-call datasource cap would scope it

error-handling asymmetry between sibling channels: perf_advice wraps JSqlParser in runCatching (SqlPerfAnalyzer.kt:122, catches Throwable) while check_sql and rollback_plan catch only Exception (UnboundedWriteDetector.kt:162, RollbackSqlGenerator.kt:133) — unifying on fatal-passthrough semantics with an input cap would make the four channels consistent

schema context output has a per-cell 200-char cap but no per-table column cap (McpSchemaFormatter.format emits every column of each returned table), so very wide tables dominate output; a per-table column budget would bound it

UnboundedWriteDetector.parseStatementsShared single AST slot is @Volatile and shared between the UI EDT confirm flow and the MCP dispatcher thread; content-equality check before reuse prevents wrong-AST reuse today, but any future consumer that mutates nodes would need to leave the shared slot first (existing hard constraint documented at UnboundedWriteDetector.kt:79-82)

surface: Dialog/preview HTML rendering of driver notices, advice text, error and SQL content; feedback server message
boundary: HTML rendering boundary: per-dialog escapeHtml variants of inconsistent completeness on lower-trust strings

local_checks.invariant: Every distinct escapeHtml/escape implementation that feeds a Swing <html> label escapes enough metacharacters for the exact HTML context it is used in
local_checks.result: Full inventory: CommunityDialog.kt:137-138 escapes &,<,>," (recon claim that it 'only escapes &' is disproved by source); ExplainPlanResultView.kt:260-261, ExplainPlanDialog.kt:120-121, RollbackSqlDialog.kt:1020-1021, and SqlResultPanel.kt inline escapes (:253,:274,:341,:446) and SqlPreviewPanelParamPanel.kt:87-89 escape &,<,> only. None escape single quotes, but no site places lower-trust text into an attribute; all sinks are element-content contexts where &<> suffices, so the inconsistent completeness is not itself exploitable. HtmlReportFormatter.kt:126 and DiagnosticReportFormatter.kt:260 (share/format) have their own escapeHtml for HTML report exports, outside the Swing surface.

local_checks.invariant: Driver notices (remote-DB WARNING/NOTICE), EXPLAIN-derived hint target/advice, and diff/baseline strings are escaped before reaching HTML JBLabels in ExplainPlanResultView
local_checks.result: raw.notices (driver notices from the remote DB) and hint.target/hint.advice (derived from remote EXPLAIN output) are escaped with &<> at :102 and :214 and land in element content of JBLabel — adequate. renderCompareLines output is escaped at :117. Baseline labels going into JComboBox (:121) are plugin bundle/build-time strings (ExplainPlanHistorySession.kt:45-61), not HTML-rendered. headerLabel (:72-81) interpolates dialectName and dataSourceName unescaped inside <html>, but both are operator-configured/plugin-constant values (same principal), so no boundary crossing there.

local_checks.invariant: Lower-trust strings (SQL fragments from console-captured statements, mapper XML identifiers, DB server error text) must be escaped or HTML-disabled before reaching HTML-enabled Swing labels and tooltips
local_checks.result: Three unescaped HTML sites found, all with lower-trust inputs: (1) RollbackSqlDialog.kt:626 interpolates $shown (currentResult.snapshotSelectSql, built at RollbackSqlGenerator.kt:283 as 'SELECT * FROM $table WHERE $whereText;' from the JSqlParser-parsed original statement, i.e. console-captured/pasted SQL text) into '...$shown' on a plain JBLabel (:85), while the same class has an unused-at-this-site escapeHtml (:1020); (2) SqlPreviewPanelResultView.kt updateMeta (:619-655) composes result.tableName, xmlModel.statementId, parser warning text and stack-digest inline text unescaped into metaCoreText/metaLineText which fullDisplayText (:728) wraps in and applyMetaTruncation (:719) writes to metaLabel — SqlPreviewPanel.kt:145 creates metaLabel as JBLabel() without the html.disable client property; (3) SqlResultPanel.kt:277 escapes the visible error label but assigns the raw error string (SQLException text from the remote DB) unescaped to infoLabel.toolTipText, which Swing renders as HTML whenever the text starts with ''. The codebase's own control — putClientProperty("html.disable", true) — is applied at only five components (DegradationBanner.kt:57, SqlPreviewPanel.kt:664 (dmlImpactBannerLabel only), SqlSelectionDialog.kt:119, CrudSqlPreviewFlow.kt:111, LogToSqlPanel.kt:739), none of them the affected labels. Swing HTML in JLabel/tooltip cannot execute script and JLabel has no HyperlinkListener, so the claimed effect is bounded to HTML layout/content injection plus resource loading (http(s) fetch or file: reference) — not code execution or clickable-link navigation.

local_checks.invariant: Feedback server response fields (message, non-JSON body snippets) and attachment naming cannot reach an HTML sink or local file naming
local_checks.result: serverMessageOf/describeHttpFailure (FeedbackApi.kt:100-133) and parsePostResponse/parseUploadResponse error text flow to ErrorReportDialog fields.statusLabel, which is a JBTextArea (ErrorReportDialog.kt:848) — plain text, no HTML rendering, so server-controlled message cannot inject HTML. Response reads are bounded: HttpRequestsSender.readBounded caps both raw and gzip-decompressed output at 2MB (FeedbackApi.kt:300-329), truncated output degrades to the nonJsonHint path. Upload attachment name is the fixed constant STACK_ATTACHMENT_NAME='sql-visualizer-stacktrace.txt' with fixed mimeType text/plain (FeedbackApi.kt:44, ErrorReportDialog.kt:350, BatchSubmitter.kt:73); the server-returned fileName/key in parseUploadResponse (:197-198) only round-trips inside the PostRequest JSON and is never used for local file naming or path construction. detailUrl (:165) interpolates postNo into a URL handed to a browser as a query parameter, not fetched by plugin code.

local_checks.invariant: HTMLEditorProvider.openEditor/JCEF page content is limited to plugin constants; no settings or theme text can carry HTML metacharacters into the JCEF page
local_checks.result: SqlLogPanel.kt:1381-1406 (HelpAction.openLocalHtml) loads the bundled resource html/marketplace-custom-page.html and performs only a boolean-themed class injection replacing <body> with <body class="dark"> (ignoreCase, from JBColor.isBright()); no user/setting/remote text is interpolated. JCEF absent falls back to BrowserUtil.browse of the constant HELP_DOCUMENTATION_URL. Settled: the injected content is purely plugin constants.

surface: Integrity- and randomness-sensitive decisions across the repo
boundary: Integrity boundary: update artifact authentication, agent frame integrity, CRC32 naming, secret handling

local_checks.invariant: Update artifact authentication: signature absent — verify compensating controls on the download-to-install path
local_checks.result: No artifact signature (peer-documented, not re-classified here). Compensating controls verified in source: fixed HTTPS manifest URL with only a launcher-controlled system-property override (UpdateSource.kt:46-48, read once at class init); UpdateZipGuard enforces per-entry and total uncompressed caps plus declared-size/CRC lying detection; DynamicInstallSupport validates the zip's META-INF/plugin.xml (bounded read) and requires <id> to equal PLUGIN_ID and <version> non-empty before install; restart-script fallback (PlatformPluginInstaller) reuses the same validated zip and unzips into the plugin root. Remaining gap (forged but plugin-id-matching artifact from a compromised update source) is the peer-owned boundary; no new candidate here.

local_checks.invariant: Agent frame integrity: no MAC on frames — verify compensating controls
local_checks.result: No MAC/HMAC on 4-byte-length frames (peer-documented; AgentProtocol.kt has no auth field). Compensating controls in source: IDE binds ServerSocket(0, backlog, InetAddress.getLoopbackAddress()) only (AgentManager.kt:791, 898) so remote processes cannot reach it; 1MB frame cap with discard-on-oversize (AgentProtocol.MAX_FRAME_LEN, AgentSessionSupport.kt:459); CONFIG channel effects limited to capture disable/desensitize/skip-prefixes. HELLO pid is self-reported by any loopback local process — that spoofing risk is the peer-owned IPC boundary; recorded here as compensating-control assessment only.

local_checks.invariant: CRC32-named agent jar temp files must not create an integrity decision
local_checks.result: extractPremainAgentJar (AgentManager.kt:1225-1259) uses CRC32 of content purely as a deterministic name for reuse, not as integrity verification. Reuse fast-path accepts an existing file whose length matches the resource — a preplaced same-length file in the plugin temp dir would be handed to -javaagent, but writing there requires the same OS user (no trust boundary crossed); the .tmp write + ATOMIC_MOVE(REPLACE_EXISTING) converges on a complete file. Hardening (use File.createTempFile-unique name or hash+size re-read), not a finding.

local_checks.invariant: No weak randomness for security-relevant values (ports, temp files, tokens)
local_checks.result: No java.util.Random and no token/nonce generation anywhere in src/main or agent main (grep Random). Agent channel ports are OS-assigned ephemeral via ServerSocket(0) on loopback; temp files use File.createTempFile or content-derived names. No security-relevant randomness decision exists to weaken.

local_checks.invariant: SHA-256 usage must be appropriate for its role (dedup/fingerprint identity, not authentication)
local_checks.result: All SHA-256 uses are unkeyed fingerprints/dedup keys over non-adversarial inputs (error fingerprint prefix, SQL-template keys, preview-origin scope hashing, autosave payload revision hash) where collision resistance of SHA-256 is the correct and sufficient property; none is used as a MAC or password verifier. No misuse.

local_checks.invariant: No homemade crypto; encoding must not be presented as integrity
local_checks.result: Base64 is used strictly as transport encoding for autosave payloads (SqlLogParamCodec documents the charset-collision rationale); reader decodes without treating it as authentication. No Cipher/Crypto usage in the codebase at all; no Base64-as-signing. No finding.

local_checks.invariant: Secrets/parameter values must not reach logs via audit or WARN paths
local_checks.result: McpAuditLog clips every audit line to 120 chars with a documented no-credential/no-parameter-value policy (only SQL text head + dataSource/dialect names). FeedbackApi logs nothing sensitive. One hardening gap: AgentSessionSupport.kt:493 logs head=${body.take(120)} of an unparseable EVENT frame into idea.log — captured SQL with literal parameter values can reach the local log; same-principal local file, display masking does not apply there. No boundary-crossing secret leak found.

hunter_hardening: AgentSessionSupport.kt:493 logs the first 120 chars of an unparseable EVENT frame body (which can contain captured SQL with literal parameter values) into idea.log; consider logging only frame length and drop reason.

UpdateSource.MANIFEST_URL_OVERRIDE (mpvs.update.manifest.url) redirects the self-update channel with no warning UI beyond one INFO log (UpdateSource.kt logOverrideIfAny); it is launcher-controlled (same principal), but a settings-page indicator of an active override would make a hijacked launch script visible.

surface: Remote update manifest host (Gitee raw) and the system-property override mpvs.update.manifest.url
boundary: Update trust chain: manifest URL -> download -> validation -> dynamic code install into the IDE

local_checks.invariant: Only an authorized principal can point the update chain at a non-default manifest URL (mpvs.update.manifest.url override, read once at object init UpdateSource.kt:46-47)
local_checks.result: Override is a JVM system property fixed at process start; the only in-repo writers are IDE vmoptions/launcher config, i.e. the same desktop principal as the operator. No repo code path (settings, MCP, history import, feedback) writes this property. No cross-principal flip found; default stays Gitee HTTPS raw URL.

local_checks.invariant: downloadUrl from the manifest is constrained before being fetched (scheme/host allowlist, HTTPS-only, redirect target bounds)
local_checks.result: downloadUrl is used verbatim in HttpRequests.request(url).saveToFile (UpdateApi.kt:66-73); no scheme or host restriction, redirects followed by default. However the only source of downloadUrl is the manifest itself, so any restriction added here is redundant with the already-documented missing-artifact-signature root cause (channel control implies arbitrary payload). Recorded as hardening, not a separate finding.

local_checks.invariant: Version comparison cannot be tricked into installing an equal-or-lower version, and comparison failure fails closed
local_checks.result: check() requires VersionComparator.compare(manifest.version, currentVersion) > 0 (PluginUpdateRunner.kt:86); null current version yields VERSION_UNREADABLE failure; any comparator exception degrades to 0 = UpToDate (VersionComparator.kt:34). Downgrade/rollback acceptance not present; a higher version claim requires manifest control, subsumed by the channel root cause. No exploitable comparator trick found in the wrapper.

local_checks.invariant: Ignore-list persistence cannot be manipulated across a trust boundary
local_checks.result: ignoreVersion joins manifest.version raw into a ';'-joined string, so a version containing ';' can inject extra entries, and isVersionIgnored matches raw strings. Impact is limited to suppressing auto-check notifications for attacker-chosen versions — an attacker who controls the manifest can simply ship a higher version; no notification-suppression-resistant state or privilege effect. Excluded as no cross-boundary impact.

local_checks.invariant: Validation of the artifact happens before any state-changing action (unload, unpack, delete command), and hot-swap failure leaves a recoverable state
local_checks.result: doInstall order: validateArtifact (step 1, DynamicInstallSupport.kt:60) → dev guard → platform probe → allowLoadUnload veto → loadDescriptorFromArtifact → unload-then-install on EDT (:237-269); any failure falls back to the restart-script path which schedules Delete+Unzip (PlatformPluginInstaller.kt:38-65). Unload never precedes validate. Unload-succeeded/load-failed is repaired by the fallback script. Ordering invariant holds.

local_checks.invariant: TOCTOU between download, guard/validate, and platform extraction does not let a lower-trust local principal swap the artifact
local_checks.result: Downloaded zip lives in a user temp file and is copied to system/mpvs-update with REPLACE_EXISTING; any local process that can swap these files runs as the same OS user as the IDE. Per candidate gate rule 3 this is a same-principal action, not a privilege gain; excluded.

local_checks.invariant: Restart-script command construction cannot be influenced into arbitrary delete/extract targets
local_checks.result: DeleteCommand target derives from the running plugin's ProtectionDomain codeSource (self path) with fallback to PathManager.getPluginsDir()/INSTALL_DIR_NAME; UnzipCommand source is the persisted self-download and target is PathManager.getPluginsDir() — all fixed/self-derived, no manifest or zip field reaches command construction. persistZip file name comes from the plugin's own temp file name. No injection sink found.

local_checks.invariant: autoCheckUpdate cannot be enabled by a lower-trust principal and startup check is single-shot
local_checks.result: autoCheckUpdate defaults false (PluginSettings.kt:248), only flipped through the settings state (same principal); StartupUpdateCheck registered as postStartupActivity (plugin.xml:387) with app-level alreadyChecked guard. Notification content: changeNotes lines are escaped (&, <, >) but the manifest.version interpolated via update.notification.versionLine is not escaped and the version field has no length cap — informational-level inconsistency only, subsumed by channel-control prerequisite; recorded as hardening.

local_checks.invariant: The plugin-id match in validateArtifact binds the installed artifact to this plugin's identity and cannot be desynced from what the platform XML parser actually reads
local_checks.result: checkDescriptorXml extracts the id with regex <id>(.*?)</id> DOT_MATCHES_ALL over the raw descriptor text (DynamicInstallSupport.kt:182-183); the regex scans inside XML comments, processing instructions, and any pre-XML text, while the platform descriptor loader (loadDescriptorFromArtifact, :88,222-227) parses real XML and ignores comments. A plugin.xml whose only matching <id>...</id> before the real element sits inside a comment passes the gate while the platform reads a foreign id — the gate and the consumer disagree. The dynamic path passes the zip and the platform-parsed descriptor straight to installAndLoadDynamicPlugin (:258-266) with no id comparison of its own. Candidate recorded.

unresolved: Platform behavior (PluginInstaller.installAndLoadDynamicPlugin / PluginDescriptorLoader / duplicate-id conflict handling) when the installed artifact's real parsed plugin id differs from cn.song.mybatisplus.visualizer.mybatis-plus-sql-visualizer is not visible in this repository's source.

surface: Downloaded update ZIP archive (content not authenticated beyond TLS)
boundary: Archive/install boundary: zip-slip, lying headers, entry bounds, install path derivation, plugin-id match

local_checks.invariant: Decompression amplification and lying headers are bounded before any platform extractor sees the archive
local_checks.result: UpdateZipGuard.check enforces 64 entries / 64MB single / 128MB total on declared sizes, then reads every non-directory entry truncated at declared+1 bytes (or 64MB+1 when size is -1), rejecting both read-over-cap and read exceptions (UpdateZipGuard.kt:48-104). It runs in downloadAndInstall before install (PluginUpdateRunner.kt:124-130) and both UI entry points route through downloadAndInstall. Worst-case plugin-side cost is bounded CPU/memory. Bounded and correctly wired; existing UpdateZipGuardTest covers normal, lying-header, entry-count, single-cap, total-cap, and orchestration-rejection cases.

local_checks.invariant: Nested-jar scanning inside the artifact is bounded
local_checks.result: validateArtifact scans at most 64 outer entries (guard upstream) and MAX_INNER_ENTRIES=2000 entries per lib jar, reading only a matched META-INF/plugin.xml with a 1MB bounded read (DynamicInstallSupport.kt:131-146,152-166,185-188); unmatched inner entries are only header-walked by ZipInputStream, not inflated. Duplicate outer entry names do not increase bounds; getEntry deterministically returns the central-directory first match. Bounded.

local_checks.invariant: Extraction entry names are canonicalized (no zip-slip via ../, absolute/drive paths, Windows colons/ADS, reserved device names, trailing dots) before any file is written outside the plugins root
local_checks.result: UpdateZipGuard validates only entry counts and sizes — it never inspects entry.name. Actual extraction is performed entirely by platform code: StartupActionScriptManager.UnzipCommand (PlatformPluginInstaller.kt:57-59) and the dynamic unpack inside PluginInstaller.installAndLoadDynamicPlugin (DynamicInstallSupport.kt:258-266); both extractors live in the IntelliJ platform jars, outside this repository, so their entry-name canonicalization behavior is not source-visible here. The plugin therefore delegates the zip-slip half of the archive/install boundary to an unverified platform guarantee: UpdateZipGuard catches lying headers and amplification but no plugin-side control rejects a malicious entry name, and no repo test exercises extraction of a traversal-named entry. Candidate recorded.

local_checks.invariant: The install path is derived from trusted constants, not from archive-controlled content (install path derivation half of the boundary)
local_checks.result: The UnzipCommand target is fixed at PathManager.getPluginsDir() (PlatformPluginInstaller.kt:106) and the dynamic path delegates layout to the platform, but neither UpdateZipGuard nor validateArtifact binds the zip's top-level directory name to UpdateSource.INSTALL_DIR_NAME. A channel-controlled zip whose top-level directory is another installed plugin's directory is extracted into that directory on the restart path (DeleteCommand only removes the visualizer's own dir/jar, PlatformPluginInstaller.kt:44-49), i.e. the archive can select which directory under the plugins root it lands in. Whether this results in overwriting another plugin's code or a duplicate-id conflict is platform behavior not visible in this repository; folded into the entry-name/identity candidate rather than reported separately.

unresolved: Whether StartupActionScriptManager.UnzipCommand and the PluginInstaller dynamic unpack canonicalize entry names (../, absolute/drive paths, NTFS colons/ADS, reserved device names, trailing dots) and fail closed on Windows is not observable in this repository's source.
Platform overwrite/conflict semantics when an update zip's top-level directory name matches another installed plugin's directory are not observable in this repository's source.

surface: OGNL test expressions inside mapper XML <if test=...> attributes
boundary: Interpreter boundary: custom OGNL subset evaluator over lower-trust mapper expressions and bindings

local_checks.invariant: The custom OGNL evaluator cannot reach any object/class beyond the provided binding map and staticFieldValues (no reflection, no @class@method dispatch, no arbitrary method invocation on binding values)
local_checks.result: Verified closed. RootRef evaluates to bindings[name] only (Ognl.kt:480); StaticFieldRef evaluates to staticFieldValues[key] only with no Class.forName (Ognl.kt:481); method dispatch is a closed whitelist (method(), Ognl.kt:596-624) plus getter-name inference that routes back into property(), which only handles MockObject/Map/Collection/Array/CharSequence and never calls reflectively (Ognl.kt:573-593). grep of the xml package for reflect/Class.forName/getMethod/invoke found nothing. parseStaticFieldRef rejects '@class@method()' (trailing '(' is 'unexpected trailing token'); assignment/ternary/lambda/new are all parse errors. Root-level identifier followed by '(' (Ognl.kt:965-967) still resolves via bindings + whitelist. Index access uses getOrNull (no OOB). No path from a mapper-authored test/bind/${} expression to arbitrary code or objects outside the bindings map.

local_checks.invariant: Expression parsing/evaluation failure is exception-safe: Ognl.kt documents '求值期异常安全降级为 EvalResult.Err' (Ognl.kt:152), so any malformed/hostile expression degrades to Err and never throws out of the render path
local_checks.result: Candidate: the confinement is incomplete. Lexer.number() calls raw.toLong() (Ognl.kt:686) which throws java.lang.NumberFormatException for integer literals exceeding Long.MAX_VALUE (20+ digits, e.g. '99999999999999999999', realistic as large timestamp/snowflake constants); parseUncached catches only OgnlParseException (Ognl.kt:133-137), parse() adds no confinement (Ognl.kt:124-131), and evaluate(text,...) calls parse outside the Throwable-guarded AST evaluator (Ognl.kt:153-157 vs 160-165), so NFE escapes. For the same reason StackOverflowError from the mutually recursive parseOr..parsePrimary descent (Ognl.kt:771-995, no depth cap) escapes on deeply nested parentheses. The exception propagates through XmlPreviewModel.from (rootPaths/classifyDetail parse at XmlPreviewModel.kt:297,333) and renderSql (TextSqlNode.kt:44, IfSqlNode.kt:69, ForeachSqlNode.kt:61) into callers that do not catch it: SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool catches only XmlParseException (SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:95) before calling renderSql (:117), and ui/XmlPreviewService.toResult calls renderSql unguarded (:257). See candidate record.

local_checks.invariant: Evaluator operator semantics match real MyBatis OGNL (OgnlOps) closely enough that rendering decisions (bind values, ${} substitution, foreach collections) do not silently diverge from real engine behavior
local_checks.result: Fidelity divergences exist beyond the 6 registered known differences (P0/P14/P15/P16/P20/P30 in RealEngineFidelityTest and docs/调研报告/20260919-T-FidelityEval-自研与真引擎已知差异清单.md): (a) cross-type equality — real OGNL OgnlOps numerically converts operands so '1' == 1 is true, this evaluator returns false (equal(), Ognl.kt:526-531: only Number-vs-Number or identity); (b) relational '</>' on non-numeric strings — real OGNL converts to double (throwing on non-numeric), this evaluator does lexical CharSequence comparison (compare(), Ognl.kt:534-539); (c) 'in' on a String is substring membership here (contains(), Ognl.kt:565-571). Production impact is bounded: XmlPreviewModel.renderSql sets conditionOverrides for every collected condition id (XmlPreviewModel.kt:164-172), so <if test> expressions are toggle-driven and are NOT OGNL-evaluated on the production panel/MCP-simulate paths; the divergence surface is <bind> values, ${} tokens, and null-mocked foreach collections. Same-principal preview-fidelity issue rather than a privilege/SQL-injection boundary failure, so recorded as hardening for the fidelity governance doc, not a security candidate.

local_checks.invariant: Resource bounds on expression parsing (cache growth, recursion depth) are adequate for lower-trust mapper-authored expressions
local_checks.result: parseCache is capped at 1024 entries with clear-all overflow (Ognl.kt:121-131, PARSE_CACHE_MAX), but cache keys have no per-expression length bound, so up to 1024 expressions of unbounded length (mapper text size) can be retained per process — low impact, hardening only. Parser/evaluator recursion depth is unbounded; this feeds the exception-confinement candidate (StackOverflowError escape). No other unbounded loops found in Lexer/Parser (single pass, no backtracking).

hunter_hardening: SecureXml pre-scan bounds only per-entity expansion; document-total expansion from repeated body references (~800 refs of a 65,536-char literal) is accepted and relies on the JDK totalEntitySizeLimit=50M backstop (documented residual boundary 4 in docs/开发计划/20260919-0501-T-XmlDtdHardening-*.md). Defense-in-depth: count '&name;' occurrences in the document body (text + attribute values) in checkEntityExpansion and reject when bodyRefs * maxEntityEstimate exceeds a total budget, removing reliance on the JDK runtime limit.

OGNL operator semantics diverge from real OGNL OgnlOps in ways not registered in docs/调研报告/20260919-T-FidelityEval-自研与真引擎已知差异清单.md: cross-type equality ('1' == 1 is true in real OGNL, false here, Ognl.kt:526-531), relational comparison of non-numeric strings (lexical here vs numeric-conversion/NFE in real OGNL, Ognl.kt:534-539), and 'in' on a String as substring membership (Ognl.kt:565-571). Production rendering of <if test> is toggle-driven (XmlPreviewModel.kt:164-172) so impact is limited to bind/${}/foreach-null evaluation, but these should be registered as known differences or aligned with OgnlOps to prevent silent preview-vs-runtime SQL divergence.

OgnlEvaluator.parseCache (Ognl.kt:121-131) caps entry count (1024, clear-all on overflow) but has no per-expression length bound; adversarial mapper text can retain up to 1024 unbounded-length expression strings per process. A per-key length cap (e.g. skip caching above a few KB) would bound it.

SecureXml entity estimator treats '%name;' inside general entity values as PE 'included in literal' expansions; where the referenced name is declared as a general entity rather than a parameter entity the JDK rejects the document, so the mismatch direction is fail-closed over-counting — no action needed beyond awareness if the estimator is ever retuned.

surface: Mapper XML files and XML snippets from project files, MCP tools, and UI preview
boundary: XML parsing boundary: XXE features, entity expansion pre-scan bypass, DOCTYPE handling, DTD resolution

local_checks.invariant: All XML parsing in the plugin funnels through SecureXml.parse (hardened DocumentBuilderFactory); no raw parser or XML-parsing library bypasses it
local_checks.result: Verified: grep of src/main (*.kt, *.java) found no DocumentBuilderFactory/SAXParserFactory/XMLInputFactory/XMLStreamReader/SAXBuilder/dom4j usage outside xml/SecureXml.kt. Only two call sites invoke SecureXml.parse: XmlMapperParser.parseDocument (src/main/kotlin/cn/song/mybatisplus/visualizer/xml/XmlMapperParser.kt:190-192) and PagesXmlParser.parseDocument (src/main/kotlin/cn/song/mybatisplus/visualizer/xml/PagesXmlParser.kt:96-98). Annotation <script> parsing (AnnotationSqlParser.kt:43), cross-namespace include reparse (XmlIncludeExpander.kt:136), PSI-side fragment resolution (psi/XmlCrossNsFragmentResolver.kt:60,106), and the MCP mapper-check tool (mcp/SqlVisualizerMapperCheckTool.kt:94) all reuse XmlMapperParser and therefore the hardened boundary. The only JDOM usage is XMLOutputter (serialization) in history/ExplainPlanSnapshot.kt:44, not parsing. Regex/string-based extraction (XmlDirectText.unwrapCdata, XmlEwExpander, TokenParser) operates on DOM-extracted text or rendered SQL, not raw untrusted XML structure, so no regex-vs-parser desync path into SQL rendering was found.

local_checks.invariant: The hand-written internal-subset splitter (internalSubset) agrees with the real JAXP parser about where the DOCTYPE internal subset begins/ends, so the expansion pre-scan cannot be desynchronized into under-scanning (invisible declarations/references)
local_checks.result: Attacked the state machine (SecureXml.kt:283-337) with the assigned vectors; no under-scan desync survived source review: (1) quotes are only legal in literals/comments/PIs in a DTD internal subset, and the splitter checks comment/PI branches before the quote branch, so quote-skipping cannot swallow markup the JDK would see (and any raw quote outside a literal is rejected by JDK = fail-closed); (2) char references are only expanded inside entity values and always shrink (>=4 chars -> <=1 char), so they cannot hide length from the estimator, and '#' is excluded from isNameChar so '&#NN;' is never miscounted as a reference; (3) conditional sections <![INCLUDE[/IGNORE[ and CDATA in the internal subset are invalid XML that JDK rejects outright, so the splitter's structural skipping of them is fail-closed over-approximation; (4) a first non-comment/non-PI/non-CDATA '<!DOCTYPE' is the only one JDK accepts (duplicate DOCTYPE rejected), so indexOfDoctype's first-match rule cannot be preempted by a legal alternative; (5) ']' + optional whitespace + '>' matches JDK's ']' S? '>' ending; a ']' inside entity values/comments/PIs is skipped by the same branches JDK uses; (6) PE substitution (visibleSubset) substitutes %name; outside comments/PIs and inside entity values, matching spec 'included in literal' semantics, with round/size caps failing closed; (7) putIfAbsent first-declaration-wins matches XML spec 4.2. Mismatches found are all in the over-counting (false-reject) direction, which fails closed. The previously found bypasses (decoy ']>', fake preamble DOCTYPE, PE smuggling, non-ASCII names, PI-carried declarations) are closed by T-XDH-07 code and pinned by SecureXmlTest.

local_checks.invariant: Entity expansion pre-scan (checkEntityExpansion) bounds entity expansion (declaration count 64 / reference depth 16 / per-entity expansion estimate 65,536 chars) so no crafted internal subset can cause unbounded expansion before JAXP parses
local_checks.result: Estimator verified: memoized per-entity expansion with cycle guard (fail on revisit), saturation at MAX+1 for chars/depth, order-independent depth criterion, diamond-DAG reuse not misflagged (pinned by SecureXmlTest). Residual gap identified and assessed: the three criteria bound per-entity expansion but not document-total expansion from repeated references in the document body (e.g. one 65,536-char literal entity referenced ~800 times in body text passes all three criteria); this is explicitly registered as residual boundary item 4 of docs/开发计划/20260919-0501-T-XmlDtdHardening-*.md with a measured JDK backstop (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING totalEntitySizeLimit=50,000,000 rejects at ~800 references, JAXP00010004), so worst-case expansion is bounded at ~50MB per parse. Accepted, documented boundary with a JDK-side control the code enables (SecureXml.kt:161); recorded as hardening, not a candidate.

local_checks.invariant: ThreadLocal factory/builder caching (T-PS6-03) does not weaken or stale the security configuration, and the pre-scan cannot be skipped via the cache
local_checks.result: Verified: cache is only used on the DEFAULT_ON_UNSUPPORTED identity path (SecureXml.kt:123-156); all security features are constants applied at factory construction (SecureXml.kt:158-168) and never mutated afterwards; entityResolver is set on every builder; checkEntityExpansion runs textually on every parse call before the builder is touched (SecureXml.kt:116-120), independent of the cache, and SecureXmlFactoryCacheTest pins that an over-limit payload is rejected on repeated parses. No staleness path that re-enables external entities/DOCTYPE denial or skips the pre-scan was found. Custom-callback (test/collector) path always builds fresh, so feature-degradation warnings are not suppressed by the cache.

OGNL operator semantics diverge from real OGNL OgnlOps in ways not registered in docs/调研报告/20260919-T-FidelityEval-自研与真引擎已知差异清单.md: cross-type equality ('1' == 1 is true in real OGNL, false here, Ognl.kt:526-531), relational comparison of non-numeric strings (lexical here vs numeric-conversion/NFE in real OGNL, Ognl.kt:534-539), and 'in' on a String as substring membership (Ognl.kt:565-571). Production rendering of <if test> is toggle-driven (XmlPreviewModel.kt:164-172) so impact is limited to bind/${}/foreach-null evaluation, but these should be registered as known differences or aligned with OgnlOps to prevent silent preview-vs-runtime SQL divergence.

OgnlEvaluator.parseCache (Ognl.kt:121-131) caps entry count (1024, clear-all on overflow) but has no per-expression length bound; adversarial mapper text can retain up to 1024 unbounded-length expression strings per process. A per-key length cap (e.g. skip caching above a few KB) would bound it.
